It has a total of 22 members—15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha. Committee on Public Undertakings – It examines the reports, accounts and functioning of public undertakings. It also has 22 members—15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha. The Joint Committee on Salaries and Allowances of Members of Parliament is a committee related to the rules regarding the salaries, allowances and facilities of MPs. Therefore, it is not considered a Financial Committee of Parliament.

Set 5.q: 23. With reference to the Swadeshi Movement, consider the following statements— 1. It contributed to reviving the skills of indigenous craftsmen and indigenous industries. 2. The National Council of Education was established as part of the Swadeshi Movement.
Set 5.explanation: The Swadeshi Movement played an important role in reviving Indian artisans and industries. According to the book 'The Swadeshi Movement in Bengal 1903–1908' by the famous historian Prof. Sumit Sarkar, there was a decline of 44% in the import of cotton yarn/thread, 22% in the import of cotton cloth, 68% in the import of shoes and boots and 55% in the import of cigarettes. During the Swadeshi Movement, the handloom industry, silk and textile industry, iron and steel industry, leather industry, etc., received significant encouragement. In 1906, the National Council of Education was formed, which was a major component of the Swadeshi Movement. Its objective was to strengthen national education under Swadeshi control in the literary, scientific and technical fields.

Set 5.q: 24. Which of the following Sultans did Nizamuddin Auliya refuse to meet?
Set 5.explanation: Sheikh Nizamuddin Auliya witnessed the rule of more than seven Sultans who came to power one after another, but he never went to the court of any of them. Sultan Jalaluddin Khilji was probably the first ruler who, after hearing about the greatness of Sheikh Nizamuddin, offered him some villages and expressed his desire to meet him. The Sheikh refused to meet him, saying, “There are two doors in my khanqah; if the Sultan enters through one, I will go out through the other.” Even after this, when Sultan Jalaluddin intended to meet Auliya without prior notice, Auliya’s beloved disciple Amir Khusro informed him about it. As soon as Auliya received the information, he immediately left for Ajodhan to pay homage to his guru, Baba Farid. Thus, Auliya continued to avoid meeting the Sultan directly. Some sources also mention Alauddin Khilji’s attempt to meet Auliya, but in the case of Alauddin Khilji, no such dramatic incident is found as occurred with Jalaluddin Khilji.

Set 5.q: 25. Which of the following caused a wave of public outrage, which led to the British massacre at Jallianwala Bagh?
Set 5.explanation: The term of the Defence of India Act enforced in India during the First World War was about to expire. Therefore, on the recommendations of the committee headed by Justice Sidney Rowlatt, two bills were presented in the Legislative Council. These bills provided for surveillance of suspected persons involved in seditious activities in India and for the arrest of any person for such activities without assigning any reason. These bills were passed by the Legislative Council in March 1919 as ‘The Rowlatt Act’. Indians strongly opposed this Act, and a wave of public anger arose against it. To protest against the arrest of two leaders of Punjab, Dr. Satyapal and Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew, who opposed this Act, a meeting was held at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar on 13 April 1919. While some people were addressing the gathering, unarmed Indians were fired upon indiscriminately on the orders of Brigadier-General Dyer. This brutal incident is known in history as the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre.

Set 5.q: 26. Consider the following statements— (1) The Arya Samaj was founded in 1835. (2) Lala Lajpat Rai opposed the Arya Samaj’s insistence on regarding the Vedas as infallible... (3) Under Keshab Chandra Sen, Brahmo Samaj launched movement for women’s education. (4) Vinoba Bhave worked for refugees through Sarvodaya Samaj.
Set 5.explanation: Arya Samaj was not founded in 1835 AD, but in 1875 AD in Bombay by Swami Dayanand Saraswati. Lala Lajpat Rai did not oppose the Vedic foundation of Arya Samaj; he only did not favour treating every interpretation or doctrine of Dayanand as mandatory or infallible. Under the leadership of Keshab Chandra Sen, Brahmo Samaj promoted the uplift of women and women’s education as important social reforms. After the death of Gandhiji, in 1948, Sarvodaya Samaj was formed at Sevagram on the initiative of Vinoba Bhave. Its objective was to establish a society based on Gandhian Sarvodaya, truth, non-violence and freedom from exploitation. Later, Vinoba also worked among refugees. Therefore, statements (1) and (2) are incorrect, while statements (3) and (4) are correct in the examination context.

Set 5.q: 27. Under the Sarda Act, what minimum age of marriage was prescribed for girls and boys respectively?
Set 5.explanation: In the year 1929, through the efforts of Dr. Harbilas Sarda, a resident of Ajmer and a judge, the Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929 was enacted. It was called the ‘Sarda Act’ after him. Under this Act, the minimum age of marriage was fixed at 14 years for girls and 18 years for boys.

Set 5.q: 28. The statement, “We shall either free India or die in the attempt,” is associated with which of the following?
Set 5.explanation: The given statement is related to the Quit India Movement. The Congress Working Committee Self-Government. The partition of Bengal was carried out by Lord Curzon in 1905.

Set 5.q: 29. One of the founding leaders of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association was—
Set 5.explanation: Explanation: The work of reorganizing the H.R.A. was started under the leadership of Vijay Kumar Sinha, Shiv Verma, Jaidev Kapoor, Bhagat Singh, Bhagwati Charan Vohra and Sukhdev. In a meeting held in September 1928 at Feroz Shah Kotla Ground, Delhi, the name of H.R.A. was changed to ‘Hindustan Socialist Republican Association’ (H.S.R.A.). Its main objective was to establish a socialist republican state in India.

Set 5.q: 30. Consider the following statements— 1. Sarojini Naidu was the first woman President of the Indian National Congress. 2. Badruddin Tyabji was the first Muslim President of the Indian National Congress.
Set 5.explanation: In the year 1917, Annie Besant was the first woman President of the Indian National Congress, whereas Sarojini Naidu became the first Indian woman President of the Congress in the annual session of the Indian National Congress held at Kanpur in 1925. Therefore, statement 1 is incorrect. The honour of being the first Muslim President of the Indian National Congress goes to Badruddin Tyabji. He was elected President of the third session of the Indian National Congress held in Madras from December 27 to 30, 1887. Therefore, statement 2 is correct.

Set 5.q: 31. Match List-I with List-II: A. Vrihi B. Mudga C. Yava D. Ikshu | (i) Sugarcane (ii) Rice (iii) Green gram (iv) Barley
Set 5.explanation: The correct matching is as follows List-I Vrihi Mudga Yava Ikshu – – – – – List-II Rice Green gram Barley Sugarcane

Set 5.q: 32. Match List-I with List-II: I. Lord Dalhousie II. Lord William Bentinck III. Lord Ripon IV. Lord Curzon | A. Prohibition of Sati B. Local self-government C. Partition of Bengal D. Doctrine of Lapse
Set 5.explanation: The Doctrine of Lapse is associated with Lord Dalhousie (1848–1856 AD). Through this doctrine, some important princely states such as Satara, Jaitpur, Sambalpur, Baghat, Udaipur, Jhansi and Nagpur were annexed. William Bentinck abolished the practice of Sati through the Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829. The most important work of Lord Ripon’s tenure was the Government Resolution on Local Gandhi-Irwin Pact – March 5, 1931 Execution of Bhagat Singh – March 23, 1931 Karachi Session of the Indian National Congress – March 29 to 31, Poona Pact – September 24, 1932

Set 5.q: 33. Consider the following events related to the Indian freedom struggle— (1) Gandhi-Irwin Pact (2) Karachi Session (3) Execution of Bhagat Singh (4) Poona Pact. Find the correct chronological order.
Set 5.explanation: The correct chronological order of the given events is as follows passed the ‘Quit India’ resolution at Wardha on July 14, 1942, and on August 8, 1942, the All India Congress Committee approved it in Bombay. In this context, this statement of Gandhiji is especially important: “I shall not be satisfied with anything less than complete independence. It is possible that the British Government may propose to abolish the salt tax, prohibit liquor consumption, etc., but my words will be—nothing less than freedom. I give you a mantra—‘Do or Die’. This mantra means that either we shall free India or lay down our lives in the attempt to achieve freedom.”

Set 5.q: 34. The Buddhist philosopher who first propounded the doctrine of Shunyata was—
Set 5.explanation: Nagarjuna was a great philosopher of the Madhyamaka branch of Mahayana Buddhist philosophy. He is considered the chief exponent of Shunyavada or Madhyamaka philosophy. His famous work is ‘Mula Madhyamaka-Karika’. Nagarjuna explained that the objects of the world do not have an independent and permanent existence. They arise depending on causes and conditions. In Buddhist philosophy, this is called Pratityasamutpada. Nagarjuna identified this Pratityasamutpada with Shunyata. Therefore, Shunyata does not mean that things are completely non-existent; rather, it means that they do not have any independent, unchanging nature. This is Nagarjuna’s Middle Way.

Set 5.q: 35. During whose reign did the Mongol invader Genghis Khan come to the north-western frontier of India?
Set 5.explanation: The Mongol leader Genghis Khan came to the north western frontier of India during the reign of Iltutmish. Seeking protection from the wrath of Genghis Khan, Jalaluddin Mangbarni, the son of the Khwarizm Shah, reached the Indus River. Possibly, Genghis Khan sent his envoys to Iltutmish asking him not to help Mangbarni. Therefore, Iltutmish did not give him any assistance, and when Mangbarni left India in 1223–24 AD, this problem was resolved.

Set 5.q: 36. Which of the following medieval rulers introduced the ‘Public Distribution System’?
Set 5.explanation: The Sultanate-period ruler Alauddin Khalji introduced a system related to market control and food-grain distribution in Delhi. He fixed the prices of essential commodities, including food grains, appointed officials to supervise the markets, exercised control over Banjaras and traders, and prohibited hoarding. The state also created food-grain stores, through which grain was made available in times of famine or supply crisis. Therefore, in the examination context, his system is considered a medieval arrangement similar to the public distribution system.

Set 5.q: 37. In Indian history, the date 6 April 1930 is known for—
Set 5.explanation: On April 6, 1930, Mahatma Gandhi launched the Civil Disobedience Movement at Dandi by taking a handful of salt in his hand. Subhas Chandra Bose compared Gandhiji’s campaign with Napoleon’s campaign from Elba to Paris. An English news correspondent, Brailsford, ridiculed it and said, “Can the Emperor be defeated by boiling water in a kettle?” The Statesman newspaper of Calcutta also sarcastically said, “Mr. Gandhi may go on boiling sea water until Dominion status is attained.”

Set 5.q: 38. With reference to ancient India, consider the following statements— 1. The concept of the stupa is originally a Buddhist concept. 2. A stupa was usually a repository of relics. 3. In the Buddhist tradition, a stupa was a votive or commemorative structure.
Set 5.explanation: The stupa has a very deep connection with Buddhism, but its original concept is not considered to have originated solely in Buddhism. In India, mound-like or tomb-like structures associated with the remains or memory of the dead were prevalent even before Buddhism. Therefore, statement 1 is incorrect. In Buddhism, the importance of the stupa increased especially because the relics, bones, ashes or sacred objects related to the Buddha or Buddhist saints were enshrined in it. For this reason, the stupa became a centre of reverence and veneration. Therefore, statement 2 is correct. With time, the stupa did not remain limited only to the enshrinement of relics. It also became associated with the events of the Buddha’s life, sacred places and the memory of important Buddhist personalities. Devotees performed circumambulation around the stupa, made offerings and gave donations. For this reason, in the Buddhist tradition, the stupa is also considered important as a votive and memorial structure. Therefore, statement 3 is correct. Thus, statements 2 and 3 are correct, while statement 1 is not correct. Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

Set 5.q: 39. Who among the following said, “Mahatma Gandhi, like a fleeting phantom, raises dust but raises no level”?
Set 5.explanation: On August 14, 1931, during talks in Bombay, Dr. B. R. Ambedkar said, “History tells that Mahatma Gandhi, like fleeting phantoms, raise dust, but raise no level.” It is noteworthy that there was a difference of opinion between Gandhiji and Ambedkar regarding the ‘condition of Dalits’. After separate representation was given to Dalits in the Communal Award announced by British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald, Mahatma Gandhi began a fast unto death on September 20, 1932. On September 24, the Poona Pact was signed between Ambedkar and Gandhiji’s followers.

Set 5.q: 40. Match List-I with List-II: A. Abhinav Bharat Society B. Anushilan Samiti C. Ghadar Party D. Swaraj Party | 1. Aurobindo Ghosh 2. Lala Har Dayal 3. C. R. Das 4. V. D. Savarkar
Set 5.explanation: The correct matching of List-I and List-II is as follows Abhinav Bharat Society – V. D. Savarkar Anushilan Samiti – Aurobindo Ghosh Ghadar Party – Lala Har Dayal Swaraj Party – C. R. Das

Set 5.q: 41. Match List-I with List-II: A. Vishakhadatta B. Varahamihira C. Charaka D. Brahmagupta | 1. Medicine 2. Drama 3. Astronomy 4. Mathematics
Set 5.explanation: The correct matching of List-I with List-II is as follows List-I – List-II (Person) Vishakhadatta – (Specialisation) Drama Varahamihira – Astronomy Charaka – Medicine Brahmagupta – Mathematics

Set 5.q: 42. Who is the propounder of Practical Vedanta?
Set 5.explanation: The propounder of Practical Vedanta was Swami Vivekananda. According to Vivekananda, Vedanta, as a religion, should be deeply practical so that we may be able to follow it in every part of our life. Vivekananda delivered his first lecture on Practical Vedanta in London on November 10, 1896.

Set 5.q: 43. Consider the following statements with reference to the Congress Socialist Party— 1. Formed in January 1934. 2. Because of his sympathy with socialism, Jawaharlal Nehru formally joined this party.
Set 5.explanation: In May 1934, an All India Socialist Conference was held by socialist minded Congress members at Anjuman Islamia Hall in Patna. At this conference, a draft committee was formed to establish the ‘All India Congress Socialist Party’, and it was decided to call the next All India Socialist meeting. In October 1934, the ‘All India Congress Socialist Party’ (Congress Socialist Party) was formally formed in Bombay. At the conference held in Patna, Acharya Narendra Deva was made the chairman of the draft committee and Jayaprakash Narayan was made its organising secretary. After the formal inauguration of the Congress Socialist Party in Bombay, Jayaprakash Narayan became the general secretary of the party. Jawaharlal Nehru never joined this party.

Set 5.q: 44. With reference to the Charter Act, 1813, which of the following is not correct?
options: This Act allowed Christian missionaries to come to India...
It established the sovereignty of the British Crown over the territories...
This Act ended the East India Company’s trade monopoly...
At the time of this Act, the Governor-General of Bengal was Lord Hastings.
Set 5.explanation: The Charter Act of 1813 was an important Act in the constitutional history of British India. By this Act, the general monopoly of the East India Company over Indian trade was ended. Now other British traders could also trade with India. However, the Company’s monopoly over the tea trade and trade with China continued. For this reason, option (c) is incorrect, because it states that the Company’s monopoly, including the tea trade, was ended.

Set 5.q: 45. Which of the following was/were included in the Gandhi-Irwin Pact? 1. Inviting Congress to Round Table 2. Withdrawing ordinances 3. Acceptance of Gandhiji’s suggestion for inquiry into police excesses 4. Release of prisoners against whom no charge of violence was made
Set 5.explanation: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact, also known as the ‘Delhi Pact’, was concluded in Delhi on March 5, 1931. It had the following provisions- 1. To invite the Congress to participate in the Second Round Table Conference; 2. To release political prisoners except those accused of violence. However, Gandhiji’s suggestion for conducting an inquiry into police excesses was not accepted in it, and the issue of the ordinance issued during the Non-Cooperation Movement was not mentioned in this agreement. Thus, the intended answer is option (b).

Set 5.q: 46. The earliest evidence of agriculture in the Indian subcontinent has been obtained from—
Set 5.explanation: On the basis of the latest discoveries, the site with the earliest evidence of agriculture in the Indian subcontinent is Lahuradewa, located in Sant Kabir Nagar district of Uttar Pradesh. Evidence of rice from between about 8000 B.C. and 7000 B.C. has been found here. It is noteworthy that, before this latest discovery, the site with the earliest agricultural evidence in the Indian subcontinent was Mehrgarh, located in Balochistan, Pakistan, where evidence of wheat from about 7000 B.C. has been found.

Set 5.q: 47. Match List-I with List-II: A. Treaty of Allahabad B. Treaty of Mangalore C. Treaty of Salbai D. Treaty of Madras | 1. 1782 2. 1784 3. 1769 4. 1765
Set 5.explanation: The correct matching of List-I with List-II is as follows : List-I List-II Treaty of Allahabad 1765 Treaty of Mangalore 1784 Treaty of Salbai Treaty of Madras

Set 5.q: 48. The recommendation to conduct the examination for 'Civil Services' simultaneously in England and India was made by which of the following?
Set 5.explanation: It had long been the demand of Indians that the Indian Civil Service examination should not be held only in England but also in India, so that Indian candidates could get equal opportunities. The Montagu-Chelmsford Report, 1918, emphasised increasing the participation of Indians in administration. This report suggested that, along with the recruitment system in England, a system of recruitment/appointment should also be started in India, and that 33% of recruitment to the higher posts of the Indian Civil Service should be made in India. As a result of this reform process, from 1922 onwards, the Indian Civil Service examination began to be held in India also. Initially, its centre was Allahabad, while the examination in London continued as before. Therefore, among the given options, the correct answer is the Montagu-Chelmsford Report.

Set 5.q: 49. Consider the following statements— 1. Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General to establish a regular police force... 2. The Supreme Court was established in Calcutta by the Regulating Act, 1773. 3. The Indian Penal Code was enacted in 1860.
Set 5.explanation: Lord Cornwallis was the first Governor-General who, as part of the police reform process, established a regular police force in India based on the British model, not Warren Hastings. Therefore, statement 1 is false. Under the Regulating Act of 1773, the Supreme Court was established in Calcutta in

Set 5.q: 50. The reason for the revival of revolutionary methods in Indian politics during the period 1923–28 was—
options: The increasing influence of leaders like Har Dayal and Lajpat Rai
The suspension of the Non-Cooperation Movement by Gandhiji
The rejection of Indian demands by the British
Set 5.explanation: In the year 1922, after the Chauri Chaura incident, Gandhiji suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement. This shattered the hopes of many nationalist youths, and they became dissatisfied with Gandhian non-violence and the strategy of the then national leadership, and began to look for alternative paths. In this atmosphere, revolutionary activities revived, and organisations such as the Hindustan Republican Association (H.R.A.) emerged in 1924. These youths were also influenced by the Russian Revolution, socialist ideas and other anti-colonial struggles. Therefore, the main reason for the recurrence of revolutionary methods during the period 1923-28 is considered to be the suspension of the Non-Cooperation Movement.

Set 5.q: 51. With reference to Sher Shah Suri, which of the following statement(s) is/are correct? 1. He was the creator of an excellent administrative system. 2. However, his qualities as a ruler were not more remarkable than his victories on the battlefield.
Set 5.explanation: Sher Shah Suri (1540 1545 A.D.) holds an important place among the rulers of medieval India. He was the creator of an excellent administrative system. Because of the reforms carried out by him in the field of administration, he is considered the precursor of Akbar. Therefore, statement 1 is true. As a ruler, Sher Shah’s qualities were more remarkable than his victories on the battlefield. He achieved success in some battles and also faced failure in some battles. For example, Humayun defeated the Afghans at a place called Daurah (Devra), in which Sher Shah also took part. Similarly, Sher Shah’s victory over Marwar was the result of treachery, whereas the work done by him as an administrator holds an important place in history. For example, under the revenue reforms carried out by him, the state treasury increased. Under military reforms, he strictly enforced the practice of branding horses, which had been introduced in India by Alauddin Khilji. He introduced pure gold, silver and copper coins in place of old, worn-out coins. He introduced the pure silver rupiya (178 grains) and the copper dam (about 380 grains). Similarly, Sher Shah’s judicial system also holds an unparalleled place in medieval India. Therefore, statement 2 is incorrect.

Set 5.q: 52. Match the hormones given in List-I with the items given in List-II: (A) Adrenaline (B) Estrogen (C) Insulin (D) Pheromone | 1. Anger, fear, danger 2. Attracting a mate... 3. Females 4. Glucose
Set 5.explanation: Adrenaline is called the emergency hormone. It prepares the body to respond immediately in situations such as fear, anger or danger. Estrogen is the major female sex hormone, which is related to the female reproductive system and secondary sexual characteristics. Insulin is secreted by the pancreas and controls the amount of glucose in the blood. Pheromones are chemical signals through which many organisms attract mates by means of the sense of smell. Therefore, the correct matching is A-1, B-3, C-4 and D-2.

Set 5.q: 53. By which method can a mixture of sand and naphthalene be separated?
Set 5.explanation: A mixture of sand and naphthalene can be separated by the method of sublimation. Naphthalene is a sublimable substance. In the process of sublimation, a substance changes directly from the solid state to the gaseous state without passing through the liquid state. Camphor is also a sublimable substance.

Set 5.q: 54. What function does blood perform in the body?
options: It transports oxygen throughout the body.
It helps in the digestion of food.
Set 5.explanation: Blood is the main medium for the transport of substances in the body. It contains red blood corpuscles, in which a pigment called haemoglobin is found. Haemoglobin combines with oxygen in the lungs and carries it through the blood to the tissues and cells of the body. The cells use this oxygen for energy production. Therefore, in this question, the correct function of blood is “to carry oxygen throughout the body.”

Set 5.q: 55. Which of the following statements is not correct?
options: The human ear is most sensitive to sounds of medium frequency...
The human eye is most sensitive to red colour.
The persistence of hearing is 1/10 second.
The persistence of vision is 1/16 second.
Set 5.explanation: The human ear is most sensitive to medium-frequency sounds, approximately 500–4000 Hz. The human eye is most sensitive to yellowish-green colour in normal light. The effect of a sound heard by our ears remains in our brain for one tenth of a second. If another sound is heard before one-tenth of a second has elapsed, the impressions of both sounds merge with each other and our brain cannot distinguish between them. Persistence of vision means that when an image is formed on the retina, its effect/impression remains on the retina for one-sixteenth of a second. It is clear that only the statement given in option (b) is false.

Set 5.q: 56. Statement (A): The main component of liquefied petroleum gas is methane. Reason (R): Methane can be directly used for burning in homes and factories...
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
Set 5.explanation: The given statement is incorrect, while the reason is correct. Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) is mainly a mixture of light hydrocarbons such as propane and butane. Methane is the main component of natural gas. When natural gas is supplied through pipelines to homes, commercial establishments and industrial units, it can be used directly as a fuel.

Set 5.q: 57. What is hydroponics?
Set 5.explanation: Hydroponics is a process in which plants are grown in water using a mineral nutrient solution. Plants obtain the nutrition required for their growth from this nutrient solution. For this reason, hydroponics is called “soilless plant cultivation.”

Set 5.q: 58. The worm used in vermiculture is
Set 5.explanation: Vermiculture means the rearing or cultivation of earthworms. Earthworms are used in the preparation of vermicompost. Earthworms consume organic waste and excrete it in a digested form as vermicastings. These castings and decomposed organic matter form nutrient-rich organic manure, i.e., vermicompost. Therefore, the worm used in vermiculture is the “earthworm.”

Set 5.q: 59. If the lens of the eye becomes opaque, the eye disease is called
Set 5.explanation: The lens of a normal eye is transparent, due to which light easily passes through it and reaches the retina. When this lens becomes cloudy or opaque, light does not reach the retina properly and vision becomes blurred. This condition is called cataract. In myopia, a person can see nearby objects clearly, but distant objects appear blurred. In hypermetropia, a person can see distant objects relatively clearly, but cannot see nearby objects clearly. In glaucoma, the main problem is related to damage to the optic nerve.

Set 5.q: 60. In hypermetropia, the image is formed
Set 5.explanation: A person suffering from hypermetropia can see distant objects clearly, but cannot see nearby objects clearly. In an affected person, the near point shifts farther away than the normal near point, i.e., 25 cm. In this defect of vision, the light rays coming from a nearby object are focused behind the retina; therefore, the image is formed behind the retina.

Set 5.q: 61. The working principle of a washing machine is
Set 5.explanation: In a washing machine, the drum is rotated at a very high speed to remove water from clothes. When the drum rotates, the water present in the clothes moves outward and comes out through the small holes in the drum. Due to this, the clothes become comparatively dry. This process is explained on the basis of centrifugal effect. In examinations, washing machines, cream separators and centrifuges are considered examples of the use of centrifugal force. Therefore, the correct option is (a) centrifugal force.

Set 5.q: 62. Which one of the following hormones is a female sex hormone?
Set 5.explanation: Estrone is a female hormone belonging to the estrogen group. Estrogen hormones are related to the female reproductive system, female sexual characteristics and processes such as the menstrual cycle. Testosterone is the main male sex hormone and is considered the chief member of the androgen group. Androsterone is also an androgenic steroid; therefore, it is not a female hormone. Thyroxine is a hormone related to the thyroid gland, which controls the metabolic activities of the body. Therefore, among the given options, the correct answer is estrone.

Set 5.q: 63. Statement (A): The temperature of a metal wire rises when an electric current is passed through it. Reason (R): Heat energy is released due to mutual collisions among metal molecules.
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
Set 5.explanation: The flow of electric current in a metallic wire is due to free electrons. When a potential difference is applied between the ends of the wire, these electrons move inside the metal lattice and repeatedly collide with stationary ions/atoms. Due to these collisions, the energy received from the electrical source is converted into the vibrational energy of the metal lattice. This energy appears in the form of heat and the temperature of the wire increases. This effect is called the heating effect of electric current or Joule heating. Hence, statement (A) is correct. But in the reason (R), the production of heat has been linked to the “mutual combination of metal molecules,” which is not the correct scientific reason. Therefore, reason (R) is incorrect.

Set 5.q: 64. Ethylene is used 1. In the artificial ripening of fruits 2. As an anaesthetic 3. In alcoholic fermentation. Which of the above statement(s) is/are not correct?
Set 5.explanation: Ethylene, also called ethene, is an important gaseous compound. In plants, it acts as a plant growth regulator and accelerates the process of fruit ripening. For this reason, ethylene is used for the controlled or artificial ripening of fruits such as bananas and tomatoes. Ethylene has also had historical use as an anaesthetic; therefore, statement 2 is considered correct. Ethylene does not take part in alcoholic fermentation. In this process, yeast and its enzymes convert sugar into ethanol and carbon dioxide. Therefore, statement 3 is incorrect. Hence, the correct answer is (a) only 3.

Set 5.q: 65. Which metal is present in myoglobin?
Set 5.explanation: Myoglobin is a protein found in the muscle tissues of almost all mammals and, in general, vertebrate animals. A heme group is present in its structure. An iron ion is present at the centre of the heme group. Because of this iron ion, myoglobin can bind oxygen. Therefore, the metal present in myoglobin is iron.

Set 5.q: 66. Which of the following polymers are used for making bulletproof items? I. Kevlar II. Glyptal III. Lexan
Set 5.explanation: In the manufacture of bullet-resistant items, materials are required that can withstand or disperse the energy of impact and provide protection. Kevlar is a strong aramid fibre. Its tensile strength is very high; therefore, bullet resistant jackets, helmets and body armour are made from it. Lexan is a polycarbonate polymer. Along with being transparent, it is also highly impact-resistant; therefore, it is used in bullet-resistant glass and protective panels. Glyptal is not used in bullet-resistant items. It is a cross linked polyester/alkyd resin, which is used in making paints. Therefore, among the given options, only I and III are correct.

Set 5.q: 67. Which one of the following groups of elements was primarily responsible for the origin of life on Earth?
Set 5.explanation: Some basic chemical elements have been very important for the origin and development of life on Earth. Carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus and sulphur are prominent among them. These elements play an important role in the structure of the main biomolecules of living organisms—proteins, nucleic acids, carbohydrates and lipids. Carbon is especially important because it can form long and complex chains, from which many organic compounds related to life are formed. Nitrogen is an essential component of proteins and nucleic acids, while hydrogen is associated with many biological compounds and water. Therefore, among the given options, the option containing carbon, hydrogen and nitrogen is the most appropriate.

Set 5.q: 68. Match List I with List II: A. Electron B. Proton C. Neutron D. Photon | 1. Quantum of electromagnetic radiation 2. Negatively charged particle 3. Neutral particle 4. Positively charged particle
Set 5.explanation: An electron is a negatively charged particle; therefore, it is matched with a negatively charged particle. A proton is found in the nucleus of an atom and has a positive charge. A neutron is also found in the nucleus, but it has no electric charge. A photon is the quantum of energy of light or electromagnetic radiation. Therefore, the correct matching is A-2, B-4, C-3, D-1. Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

Set 5.q: 69. Consider the following statements— (i) In the process of photosynthesis, CO2 is reduced. (ii) In the process of photosynthesis, H2O is oxidized.
Set 5.explanation: Photosynthesis is considered a redox process because both reduction and oxidation take place in it. In the process of photosynthesis, carbon in carbon dioxide (CO2 ) is in a more oxidised state, and during photosynthesis it is reduced to carbohydrate/glucose, while water (H2 O) undergoes oxidation. Therefore, both statements (i) and (ii) are correct.

Set 5.q: 70. The diffusion of light in the atmosphere is caused by—
Set 5.explanation: Sunlight is a mixture of the different colours that make up white light. When it passes through the atmosphere, it is scattered by air molecules, suspended dust particles and other fine particles present along its path. Therefore, option (b) is correct.

Set 5.q: 71. “3D printing” has applications in which of the following? 1. Preparation of confectionery items 2. Manufacture of bionic ears 3. Automotive industry 4. Reconstructive surgeries 5. Data processing technologies
Set 5.explanation: 3-D printing is a modern manufacturing technique. In this process, a digital 3D model of an object is prepared, and then the machine converts it into a real object by joining very thin layers. Therefore, it is called additive manufacturing. The scope of this technology is very wide. In the food industry, items such as chocolate, candy, sugar confectionery and cake decorations can be made using it. In the biomedical field, research has been carried out on bioelectronic organs such as bionic ears through 3-D printing. In the automotive industry, it is used for making rapid prototypes, tools and certain special parts. In reconstructive surgery, models, surgical guides and implants can be prepared according to the patient’s anatomy. Similarly, in data-processing technologies, it is related to areas such as computing and electronic components, sensors, circuits and optical computing chips. Thus, 3-D printing is used in all the given fields. Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

Set 5.q: 72. In plants, ‘phloem’ is mainly responsible for—
Set 5.explanation: The main function of phloem is to transport food prepared in the green parts of the plant to other parts. This tissue is also called bast. It is made up of four types of cells, namely sieve elements, companion cells, phloem parenchyma and phloem fibres. It should be noted that xylem is responsible for the transport of water and mineral salts in plants. Therefore, phloem is mainly responsible for the transport of food.

Set 5.q: 73. What is Vermiculture?
Set 5.explanation: The correct scientific meaning of vermiculture is the culturing or rearing of earthworms or worms. In this process, the number of earthworms is increased by providing them suitable moisture, temperature and organic matter. Earthworms make the soil loose and aerated by forming tunnels in it. They help in the decomposition of organic matter and increase the fertility of the soil. Due to this usefulness, the earthworm is called the “farmers’ friend.”

Set 5.q: 74. Consider the following statements regarding Vermiculture and Vermicomposting— 1. In vermiculture, earthworms are reared and cultured. 2. In vermicomposting, organic waste is converted into compost... 3. The earthworm belongs to the class Insecta.
Set 5.explanation: Vermiculture means the rearing and culturing of earthworms. In this process, earthworms are grown under favourable conditions. In vermicomposting, kitchen, farm and other organic waste is converted into nutrient-rich manure with the help of these earthworms. Earthworms make the soil loose and aerated and help in increasing the amount of humus in the soil. Therefore, the earthworm is called the “farmers’ friend.” The third statement is incorrect because earthworms are not insects. Earthworms belong to the phylum Annelida, whereas insects belong to the phylum Arthropoda. Therefore, the correct answer is only 1 and 2.

Set 5.q: 75. Which one of the following is not correctly matched?
options: Nautical mile – Unit of distance in navigation
Set 5.explanation: Degree Celsius is a unit used to measure temperature. Heat is a form of energy, and its SI unit is joule. The unit used to measure distance in navigation is the nautical mile. The unit of power is joule per second, which is called watt. One horsepower is approximately equivalent to 746 watts. The loudness of sound is measured in decibels. Therefore, (d) is not correctly matched.

Set 5.q: 76. Consider the following statements— 1. Inflation benefits debtors. 2. Inflation benefits bondholders.
Set 5.explanation: Statement 1 is correct because the debtor has to repay the same nominal amount later, but due to inflation, the real purchasing power of that amount decreases. Therefore, the real burden of debt decreases and the debtor gains. Statement 2 is incorrect because an ordinary bondholder receives fixed interest or fixed payments. When inflation increases, the real purchasing power of these fixed payments decreases. Therefore, ordinary bondholders do not gain; rather, they suffer a loss. The correct answer is (a).

Set 5.q: 77. Inflation can best be described as—
options: A rise in the price index
An increase in the purchasing power of money
A rise in the prices of specific goods
Set 5.explanation: Inflation refers to an increase in the general price level of goods and services in an economy. It is best expressed by an increase in the price index. Due to inflation, the purchasing power of money decreases, meaning that fewer goods and services can be purchased with the same amount of money than before. Therefore, the correct answer is (b), an increase in the price index.

Set 5.q: 78. What is the main basis of poverty estimates in India?
Set 5.explanation: Poverty in India is estimated mainly on the basis of monthly per capita consumption expenditure. While determining the poverty line, it is assessed how much a family spends on essential goods and services such as food, clothing, education, health care, etc.

Set 5.q: 79. Foreign exchange that tends to migrate rapidly is called—
Set 5.explanation: Hot money refers to short-term foreign capital or funds that move rapidly from one country to another in search of higher returns, higher interest rates, favourable exchange rates, or the possibility of speculative gains.

Set 5.q: 81. With reference to schemes related to rural development in the Union Budget 2026–27, consider the following statements— 1. ₹54,916.70 crore allocated to PMAY-Gramin. 2. ₹30,000 crore to MGNREGS. 3. ₹19,000 crore to PMGSY.

Set 5.q: 91. Consider the following statements— 1. High clouds primarily reflect solar radiation and cool the surface of the Earth. 2. Low clouds have a high absorption of infrared radiation emanating from the Earth’s surface...
Set 5.explanation: The thermal effect of clouds depends on their type, height, and thickness. Generally, low-level and thick clouds reflect more solar radiation back into space. Therefore, their main effect is to cool the Earth’s surface. High-level and thin clouds, such as cirrus clouds, allow most incoming solar radiation to pass through. However, they absorb and re-emit a part of the outgoing infrared/long-wave radiation from the Earth, which increases the heating effect. Therefore, the first statement is incorrect, because high clouds do not produce cooling as their main effect. The second statement is also incorrect, because the main effect of low clouds is not heating but cooling.

Set 5.q: 92. Consider the following rivers— (1) Vamsadhara (2) Indravati (3) Pranahita (4) Pennar. Which of the above are tributaries of the Godavari?
Set 5.explanation: The tributaries of the Godavari include the Pranhita (formed by the confluence of the Wainganga, Penganga, and Wardha rivers), Maner, Indravati, Sabari, Manjira or Manjara, Purna, Pravara, etc. Thus, the Vamsadhara and Pennar rivers are not tributaries of the Godavari. Set 5.q: 101. Which of the following statements about the laterite soils of India are correct? 1. They are generally red in colour. 2. They are rich in nitrogen and potash. 3. They are well developed in Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh. 4. Tapioca and cashew grow well in these soils.
Set 5.explanation: The red colour of laterite soil is due to iron oxide. These soils are generally rich in iron and aluminium, while they are deficient in nitrogen, potash, lime, phosphorus and organic matter. Laterite soil is mainly developed in the states of South India, the Western Ghats region of Maharashtra, Odisha, some parts of West Bengal and the north-eastern parts of the country. Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh are not major areas where these soils are well developed. These soils are generally of low fertility, but with the use of fertilizers, crops such as tea, coffee, tapioca and cashew are grown on them.

Set 5.q: 125. Recently, legendary playback singer Asha Bhosle passed away. In which year was she honoured with the country’s second-highest civilian award, the ‘Padma Vibhushan’?
Set 5.explanation: Legendary playback singer Asha Bhosle passed away in Mumbai on April 12, 2026, at the age of 92. She began her singing career in 1943 and, in a career spanning more than eight decades, lent her voice to more than 12,000 songs in over 20 Indian languages. She was honoured with the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for the year 2000 and with the Padma Vibhushan by the Government of India in 2008. The Padma Vibhushan is the country’s second-highest civilian honour after the Bharat Ratna.

Set 5.q: 126. What is the total length and construction cost of the ‘Delhi–Dehradun Economic Corridor’, recently dedicated to the nation?
Set 5.explanation: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the 213-km-long, six-lane, access-controlled Delhi Dehradun Economic Corridor in Dehradun on April 14, 2026. It has been developed at a cost of more than ₹12,000 crore. This corridor passes through Delhi, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand and will reduce the travel time between Delhi and Dehradun from more than 6 hours to about 2.5 hours. From an environmental point of view, it includes features such as a nearly 12-km-long elevated wildlife corridor, animal passes, elephant underpasses and a tunnel near the Daat Kali Temple. Therefore, the correct answer option is (b).

Set 5.q: 127. Major General Roman Gofman has recently been appointed as the new Director of the renowned intelligence agency ‘Mossad’ of which country?
Set 5.explanation: Explanation: Major General Roman Gofman was appointed the new director of Israel’s intelligence agency Mossad. On 2 June 2026, he assumed office as the 14th director of Mossad, replacing David Barnea. Before his appointment, he was the military secretary to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Set 5.q: 128. With reference to the Wisden Cricketers’ Almanack 2026 awards, which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
options: The only Indian among the Five Cricketers of the Year – Ravindra Jadeja
Set 5.explanation: In the Wisden Cricketers’ Almanack 2026, based on performances in 2025, Australia’s Mitchell Starc was named the Leading Men’s Cricketer in the World, while India’s Deepti Sharma was named the Leading Women’s Cricketer in the World. The Five Cricketers of the Year included four Indian players—Shubman Gill, Ravindra Jadeja, Rishabh Pant and Mohammed Siraj—along with England’s Haseeb Hameed. Therefore, the matching “Only Indian in the Five Cricketers of the Year – Ravindra Jadeja” is incorrect. Shubman Gill also won the Wisden Trophy for his exceptional performance of 269 and 161 runs, a total of 430 runs, in the Edgbaston Test. Wisden is often called the “Bible of Cricket.”

Set 5.q: 129. Which port, operated by Adani Ports, has become India’s largest automobile export hub by exporting 6,008 cars in a single vessel?
Set 5.explanation: Mundra Port in Gujarat, operated by Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited, became India’s leading automobile export hub after achieving the milestone of exporting 6,008 cars on a single vessel. This achievement was made possible through Mundra Port’s Roll-on/Roll-off (Ro-Ro) facility, which makes the loading and unloading of vehicles onto and off ships more efficient.

Set 5.q: 130. Indian athlete Sawan Barwal broke Shivnath Singh’s 48-year-old national record by clocking 2 hours 11 minutes 58 seconds at the Rotterdam Marathon 2026. In which year did Shivnath Singh set this record?
Set 5.explanation: Indian long-distance runner Sawan Barwal set a new Indian national record in the men’s marathon by clocking 2 hours, 11 minutes and 58 seconds at the NN Marathon Rotterdam held in the Netherlands on 12 April 2026. He broke Shivnath Singh’s old national record of 2 hours and 12 minutes. Shivnath Singh had set this record on 28 May 1978 in Jalandhar. Sawan Barwal finished 20th overall in this marathon. Therefore, the correct answer is option (b) i.e. 1978.

Set 5.q: 133. Who has become the first Indian woman chess player to win the title of the ‘FIDE Women’s Candidates Tournament 2026’ held in Cyprus?
Set 5.explanation: On 15 April 2026, Indian Grandmaster R. Vaishali won the FIDE Women’s Candidates Tournament 2026 in Cyprus by defeating Kateryna Lagno in the final, 14th round. She became the first Indian female chess player to win this title.

Set 5.q: 134. Who won the historic first gold medal for India at the 15th ‘European Girls’ Mathematical Olympiad’ (EGMO 2026), held in Bordeaux, France?
Set 5.explanation: India achieved historic success at the 15th European Girls’ Mathematical Olympiad (EGMO) 2026, held in Bordeaux, France, from 9 to 15 April 2026. Set 5.q: 135. With reference to the ecological niche, which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. It represents the range of conditions that a species can tolerate... 2. Each species has its own specific ecological role.
Set 5.explanation: An ecological niche means the ‘functional position’ or ‘role’ of a species in an ecosystem. The niche of a species is formed by all these factors—where it lives, what conditions it can tolerate, what resources it uses, what it feeds on, which organisms feed on it, and what role it plays in the community. For this reason, Statement 1 is correct, because a niche includes the conditions a species can tolerate, its use of resources and its functional role in the ecosystem. Statement 2 is also correct, because every species has its own specific ecological role.

Set 5.explanation: The correct matching is as follows SDG - 1 – No Poverty SDG - 3 – Good Health and Well-being SDG - 4 – Quality Education SDG - 6 – Clean Water and Sanitation

Set 5.q: 137. The Montreal Protocol is related to the protection of which of the following?
Set 5.explanation: The Montreal Protocol is related to the protection of the ozone layer present in the atmosphere. It is a protocol under the Vienna Convention for the Protection of the Ozone Layer. Its objective is to phase out the production and consumption of ozone-depleting substances such as CFCs. This protocol entered into force on 1 January 1989.

Set 5.q: 138. Which of the following are the most suitable crops for green manuring? 1. Sunn hemp and black gram 2. Green gram and dhaincha 3. Sugarcane and wheat
Set 5.explanation: Green manure refers to a crop that is grown in the field and ploughed back into the soil at its tender stage. This increases organic matter in the soil, enhances microbial activity and improves soil fertility. Leguminous crops are more suitable for green manure because the bacteria found in their root nodules fix atmospheric nitrogen. Sunn hemp, dhaincha, guar, cowpea, green gram (moong) and black gram (urad) are major crops used for green manure. Among these, sunn hemp and dhaincha are especially considered fast-growing and high biomass crops. Green gram and black gram are also leguminous crops and help improve the nitrogen status of the soil. On the other hand, sugarcane and wheat are main crops and are generally not considered suitable for green manure. Therefore, Statements 1 and 2 are correct, and the correct answer is option (b).

Set 5.q: 139. Which of the following is included in the in situ method of bioremediation?
Set 5.explanation: Bioremediation is a biological method of pollution control in which pollutants are degraded or converted into less harmful substances with the help of microorganisms. Composting, landfarming and bioreactor treatment are ex situ techniques of bioremediation, whereas bioventing is an in situ technique of bioremediation.

Set 5.q: 140. If the vegetation found on Earth, i.e. trees and plants, were to disappear, which gas would become deficient?
Set 5.explanation: Trees and plants, during photosynthesis, release oxygen, the life-giving gas, and absorb carbon dioxide, the gas responsible for global warming. If there is no vegetation, a shortage of oxygen will have a fatal effect on life on Earth.

Set 6.explanation: In the Vedic period, the teacher who taught the Vedas and Vedangas for earning a livelihood was called an Upadhyaya. An Acharya established a Gurukul and taught his students without charging any fee; however, he accepted the dakshina given by the student.

Set 6.q: 5. Who were not allotted separate electorates and reserved seats under MacDonald’s Communal Award?
Set 6.explanation: On 16 August 1932, British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald announced the Communal Award. In this, the system of separate electorates was not only continued for Muslims, but was also applied to the Depressed Classes. Under this, the facility of separate electorates was provided for Muslims, Indian Christians, Sikhs, Anglo-Indians, Europeans and others, and it was applicable only to the provincial legislatures. Therefore, it is clear that separate electorates and reserved seats were not allotted to Buddhists under it.

Set 6.q: 6. In Mahayana Buddhism, by what other name is Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara known?
Set 6.explanation: Avalokiteshvara is a major Bodhisattva associated with compassion in Mahayana Buddhism. He is also called Padmapani, because in this form he is shown holding a lotus in his hand. Padma means lotus and Pāṇi means hand. Therefore, the lotus-bearing form of Avalokiteshvara is called Padmapani.

Set 6.q: 7. Which of the following is false about the Congress session held at Lucknow in 1916?
options: Ambika Charan Majumdar did not preside over it.
In this session, a reunion took place between the Moderates and the Extremists.
Mahatma Gandhi was made aware of the problems of the peasants of Champaran for the first time.
Set 6.explanation: In the Lucknow Session of the Congress in 1916, the Moderates were readmitted into the Congress under the leadership of Tilak. President Ambika Charan Majumdar said, “After 10 years of painful separation and wandering in unnecessary disputes caused by misunderstandings, both groups of the Indian National Party, the Moderates and the Extremists, have now realized that separation is their defeat and unity is their victory. Now the brothers have reunited.” It was also in the Lucknow Session of the Congress that Rajkumar Shukla met Mahatma Gandhi and informed him about the problems of the peasants of Champaran. Therefore, the statement of option (a) is incorrect, while the statements of (b) and (c) are correct.

Set 6.q: 8. In the bronze images of Nataraja made during the Chola period, the divine figure is generally
Set 6.explanation: Chola artists achieved great excellence in sculpture, especially in the art of bronze casting. They made a large number of stone and metal images. More metal, especially bronze, images were made than stone images. The bronze images of Nataraja are counted among the most famous and finest creations of Chola art. These images are generally in four-armed form.

Set 6.q: 10. During whose reign was the 'Treaty of Chittor' signed between the Mughals and the Rana of Mewar?
Set 6.explanation: The Treaty of Chittor was concluded in 1615 CE during the reign of Jahangir. This treaty took place after a long struggle between the Mughals and Rana Amar Singh of Mewar. On behalf of Jahangir, Prince Khurram, who later became Shah Jahan, played a major role in the Mewar campaign. In this agreement, Rana Amar Singh accepted Mughal supremacy, but he was not compelled to appear personally in the Mughal court. His son Karan Singh was associated with the Mughal court and service. The Mughals returned to the Rana the territories of Mewar, including Chittor, which were earlier under Mughal control. However, an important condition was that Chittor Fort was not to be repaired or refortified.

Set 6.q: 11. On the death of which Muslim ruler of Delhi did a historian say, 'The king was freed from his subjects and the subjects from the king.'
Set 6.explanation: When Muhammad bin Tughlaq was in Daulatabad, a rebellion broke out in Gujarat under the leadership of Taghi. The Sultan himself went to Gujarat to suppress this rebellion. Taghi was defeated and fled to Sindh. After restoring peace and order in Gujarat, the Sultan proceeded towards Sindh to eliminate Taghi. On the way, the Sultan fell ill and died near Thatta on 20 March 1351. On his death, Badauni wrote, “The Sultan was freed from his subjects and the subjects were freed from their Sultan.”

Set 6.q: 12. With reference to the history of philosophical thought in India, consider the following statements related to the Samkhya school: 1. Samkhya does not accept the theory of rebirth or the transmigration of the soul. 2. Samkhya believes that self-knowledge alone leads to liberation...
Set 6.explanation: Samkhya is one of the major orthodox traditions of Indian philosophy. It believes in the dualism of Purusha and Prakriti. Samkhya does not reject the theory of rebirth or transmigration; rather, it accepts the idea of the transmigration of the subtle body from one body to another. Therefore, statement 1 is incorrect. According to Samkhya, the main cause of bondage is aviveka, that is, the inability to understand the difference between Purusha and Prakriti. When a person realizes that Purusha is the pure conscious witness and Prakriti is different from it, then liberation or Kaivalya is attained. Therefore, in Samkhya, self-knowledge or discriminative knowledge is considered the means of liberation, not any external influence or factor. Hence, statement 2 is correct.

Set 6.q: 13. Which of the following statements is correct with reference to the Puranas? 1. The Vishnu Purana provides information about the Maurya dynasty. 2. The Vayu Purana throws light on the administrative system of the Gupta dynasty.
Set 6.explanation: The Puranas are important literary sources of dynastic information for ancient Indian history. In the Vishnu Purana, the Mauryas are mentioned after the Nandas in the sequence of the dynasties of Magadha. It also indicates the establishment of Chandragupta in power by Kautilya and the succession of Mauryan rulers such as Chandragupta, Bindusara and Ashoka. Similarly, the Vayu Purana provides information related to the Gupta dynasty. It indicates the territorial extent or realm of Gupta rule, in which regions such as Prayag, Saketa and Magadha were important. Therefore, the second statement is also considered correct. However, the term “system of administration” should be understood here not in the sense of a detailed administrative structure, but in the sense of the territorial extent and political position of the Guptas. Thus, both statements are correct; therefore, the correct answer is option (d).

Set 6.q: 14. According to the Portuguese writer Nuniz, in which of the following fields were women skilled in the Vijayanagara Empire? 1. Wrestling 2. Astrology 3. Accounting 4. Prediction
Set 6.explanation: The Portuguese writer Fernao Nuniz visited India during the reign of Achyuta Deva Raya, the ruler of Vijayanagara. He also stayed for some time at the court of Achyuta Deva Raya. Nuniz was a horse trader. According to Nuniz, women in the Vijayanagara Empire were skilled in wrestling, astrology, accounting, prediction, music and dance. Thus, option (d) is the correct answer.

Set 6.q: 15. The earliest evidence of the availability of silver in India is found in
options: the Chalcolithic culture of Western India
Set 6.explanation: The earliest evidence of the presence of silver in India has been found in the Harappan culture. The Harappan civilization was a Bronze Age urban civilization, and its people were skilled in metallurgy. They used metals such as copper, bronze, gold and silver. Silver was used in the form of ornaments and beads. Silver objects have been found at sites such as Mohenjo-daro, Harappa and Lothal.

Set 6.q: 16. The Indian Famine Code, 1883 was framed by which of the following commissions?
Set 6.explanation: The Indian Famine Code of 1883 was associated with the Strachey Commission. The famine of 1876–78 exposed the weaknesses of the famine relief system of the British Indian administration. Thereafter, in 1878, a Famine Commission was formed under the chairmanship of Richard Strachey. This commission suggested that, in the event of famine, relief work should be carried out according to pre-determined rules, able-bodied persons should be given relief through work, incapable and destitute persons should be given free assistance, and the government should clearly discharge its responsibility for relief administration. On the basis of these recommendations, the Provisional Indian Famine Code was prepared in

Set 6.q: 17. Jammu and Kashmir became an integral part of India on
Set 6.explanation: On 26 October 1947, Maharaja Hari Singh of Jammu and Kashmir handed over the Instrument of Accession, signed for accession to India, to Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru. From 27 October 1947, the Indian Army began driving out the tribal raiders from Pakistan. Sheikh Abdullah was first given a leading role in the emergency administration, and in March 1948, under the Maharaja’s proclamation, he became the Prime Minister of the interim government.

Set 6.q: 18. With reference to 'deindustrialization', which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. This process began in 1813. 2. The end of the trading monopolies of the East India Company accelerated this process.
Set 6.explanation: ‘De-industrialization’ refers to the process in which the traditional industries, cottage industries and handicrafts of a country gradually decline, and the artisans associated with them begin to lose their livelihoods. During British rule, this process was especially visible in the textile industry in India. The Charter Act of 1813 was an important turning point in this process. This Act ended the East India Company’s monopoly over Indian trade. Although the Company’s monopoly over trade with China and the tea trade continued, the Indian market was opened to British traders to a large extent. Due to the Industrial Revolution in Britain, cheap machine-made cloth was being produced in large quantities. India became a large market for selling these goods. As a result, Indian weavers and cottage industries could not compete with cheap British machine-made goods. This accelerated the decline of Indian handicrafts and traditional industries. Therefore, both statements are correct.

Set 6.q: 19. In medieval India, what did the term 'Fanam' refer to?
Set 6.explanation: ‘Phanam’ or ‘Fanam’ was a small coin or currency unit prevalent in South India. Among medieval South Indian currencies, it was generally found as a small gold coin, and its circulation increased around the 16th century. These coins were usually made of gold.

Set 6.q: 20. Consider the following statements about the Ajivika sect: A. Makkhali Gosala was its most important leader. B. The central idea of the philosophy was 'Niyati'. C. Discrimination was practised on the basis of caste and class. D. Regular assemblies were held for the meetings of the Ajivikas.
options: B, C and D are correct.
A, B and D are correct.
More than one of the above.
Set 6.explanation: The Ajivika sect was an atheistic or materialistic sect that developed on Indian soil as one of the ancient philosophical traditions of the world. Makkhali Gosala was the most important leader of this sect, and he was a contemporary of Gautama Buddha and Mahavira Swami. The most important idea of the Ajivika philosophy was ‘Niyativada’, or determinism/ fatalism, according to which human beings have no free will. Whatever has happened, is happening, and will happen is completely predetermined and is the result of cosmic principles. The Ajivika sect did not discriminate on the basis of caste or class, and its ascetics and followers came from different sections of society. The Ajivikas held regular assemblies for discussion and planning for the future, which were part of their organizational structure and community practices. Thus, among the above statements, except statement (C), the other statements (A, B and D) are true.

Set 6.q: 22. Consider the following statements related to Madam Bhikaiji Cama: 1. Madam Cama hoisted the national flag at the International Socialist Conference held in Paris in 1907. 2. Madam Cama served as the private secretary of Dadabhai Naoroji. 3. Madam Cama’s parents were Parsis.
Set 6.explanation: Madam Cama was born on 24 September 1861. Her parents were Parsis. Sorabji Framji Patel was her father. She was married to Rustam K. R. Cama, who was a lawyer. Madam Cama served as personal secretary to Dadabhai Naoroji, one of the great pioneer leaders of the Indian national movement. Later, she came into contact with some patriotic students and European intellectuals and became associated with the freedom movement. She is famous as the ‘Mother of the Indian Revolution’. On 22 August 1907, at the Second International Socialist Congress held in Stuttgart, Germany, she hoisted the flag of Indian independence for the first time on foreign soil. The flag hoisted there was a modified form of the Calcutta Flag. Therefore, the first statement is incorrect, because this conference was held in Germany and not in Paris. The remaining two statements are correct.

Set 6.q: 23. Who is called the 'Father of Indian Archaeology'?
Set 6.explanation: Alexander Cunnin gham is called the ‘Father of Indian Archaeology’. He was a British military engineer, but during his service in India, he developed an interest in studying ancient monuments, inscriptions, coins and archaeological sites. He conducted a systematic survey of India’s ancient remains and played an important role in giving an institutional form to archaeological studies. In 1861, he became the first Archaeological Surveyor, and later served as the first Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India.

Set 6.q: 24. On the basis of the remains found in the excavation of the Harappan Civilization, which of the following are not correct? (i) Bricks of the same size were used for all types of construction work. (ii) Most houses were built as single-storeyed houses. (iii) The main roads were, on average, ten metres wide.
Set 6.explanation: In the Indus Valley Civilization/Harappan Civilization, both baked and unbaked bricks were used. The general ratio of baked bricks found in Indus cities was usually 4 : 2 : 1. Evidence of decorated bricks has been found at Kalibangan, while evidence of curved bricks has been found at Chanhudaro. Therefore, bricks of one uniform size were not used for all kinds of construction in the and Ajatashatru, the Haryanka rulers of Magadha. The second statement is Indus Valley Civilization. Hence, statement (i) is incorrect. Houses built in the Indus Valley Civilization were generally single-storeyed; however, on the basis of evidence of staircases found in some buildings, it can be said that some houses were also two-storeyed. Hence, statement (ii) is also incorrect. The average width of the main roads found in the Indus Valley Civilization was about 10 metres. Thus, statement (iii) is correct.

Set 6.q: 25. Consider the following events that occurred during India’s freedom struggle: 1. Chauri Chaura violence 2. Morley-Minto Reforms 3. Dandi March 4. Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms. The correct chronological order of the above events is
Set 6.explanation: The correct chrono logical order of the events is as follows: Minto-Morley (Morley-Minto) Reforms - 1909 Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms - Chauri-Chaura Incident - 1922 Dandi March - 1930 Thus, the correct sequence is 2, 4, 1, 3. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

Set 6.q: 26. By what name were the Maratha claims to revenue for protection known?
Set 6.explanation: ‘Chauth’ was collected from those provinces which were called ‘Mughlai’. In return for this ‘tax’, the neighbouring states received an assurance of protection from Maratha attacks and plunder.

Set 6.q: 27. The Delhi Sultan who is famous for constructing the largest network of canals in India was
Set 6.explanation: Firoz Shah Tughlaq was famous in the Delhi Sultanate for large-scale canal construction and the expansion of the irrigation system. He had canals and water structures constructed/expanded to promote agriculture in Hisar-Firoza and the Haryana-Punjab region. Major canals such as Rajabwah and Ulughkhani are mentioned; some sources also count five major canals. He imposed an irrigation tax called ‘Haqq-i Sharb’ on farmers who irrigated their fields using state-built canals. Its rate is generally stated to be 1/10 of the produce. This tax was imposed with the approval of the ulema.

Set 6.q: 28. Swami Sahajanand Saraswati published a magazine named
Set 6.explanation: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati was a prominent peasant leader of modern India. He published a journal named Hunkar.

Set 6.q: 29. Consider the following statements: 1. The mother of Vardhamana Mahavira was the daughter of Chetaka, the chief of the Licchavis. 2. The mother of Gautama Buddha was a princess of the Koliya dynasty. 3. The 23rd Tirthankara Parshvanatha was from Banaras.
Set 6.explanation: Trishala or Videha datta, the mother of Vardhamana Mahavira, was the sister of Chetaka, the chief of the Lichchhavi clan of Vaishali, and not his daughter. For this reason, from his maternal side, he was closely related to Bimbisara correct. The 23rd Tirthankara, Parshvanatha, was born in Varanasi (Banaras) about 250 years before Lord Mahavira.

Set 6.q: 30. Who among the following said, 'Ryotwari is a system which has always prevailed in India'?
Set 6.explanation: The originators of the Ryotwari system were Thomas Munro and Alexander Read. In India, the British first implemented it in Baramahal of Tamil Nadu. Under this system, the ryots were given ownership rights over land. Regarding this system, Thomas Munro said, “Ryotwari is a system which has always existed in India.”

Set 6.q: 31. In the pairs given below, the names of kings of the ancient and medieval periods are given on one side and the works composed by them on the other side. Which of these pairs is correctly matched?
Set 6.explanation: Krishnadeva Raya, the ruler of Vijayanagara, composed Amuktamalyada in the Telugu language. Mattavilasa Prahasana was composed by the Pallava ruler Mahendravarman I. Bhoja composed Samarangana Sutradhara and Someshvara composed the text Manasollasa.

Set 6.q: 32. Which one of the following statements about Dadabhai Naoroji is false?
options: He was the first Indian to be appointed Professor of Mathematics and Physics at Elphinstone College, Bombay.
In 1892, he was elected as a member of the British Parliament.
He started a Gujarati magazine, 'Rast Goftar'.
He presided over the Indian National Congress four times.
Set 6.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji was the first Indian to be appointed as Professor of Mathematics and Natural Philosophy at Elphinstone College, Bombay. From 1892 to 1895, he was a member of the British Parliament as a member of the Liberal Party. He started a Gujarati journal named Rast Goftar in 1851. Dadabhai Naoroji presided over the Indian National Congress a total of three times, in 1886, 1893 and 1906.

Set 6.q: 33. Consider the following events and arrange them in chronological order: I. Establishment of the Ghadar Party II. Chittagong Armoury Raid III. Establishment of the 'Indian Independence Committee' in Berlin IV. Central Assembly Bomb Case
Set 6.explanation: The chronological order of the given events is: Establishment of the Ghadar Party - Establishment of the ‘Indian Independence Committee’ in Berlin - 1914 Central Assembly Bomb Case - 8 April, 1929 Chittagong Armoury Raid - 18 April,

Set 6.q: 34. Muzaffar Ahmad, S. A. Dange, Shaukat Usmani and Nalini Gupta were imprisoned in connection with which conspiracy case?
Set 6.explanation: When leftist ideology gained ground in India in the third decade of the twentieth century, the government resorted to repression. Leftist leaders began to be jailed. Under this policy, in 1924, Shripad Amrit Dange, Muzaffar Ahmad, Nalini Gupta and Shaukat Usmani were jailed in connection with the Kanpur Bolshevik Conspiracy Case. All four were sentenced to four years of rigorous imprisonment.

Set 6.q: 35. Komagata Maru was
options: A political party based in Taiwan.
A peasant communist leader of China.
A ship that set out on a voyage to Canada.
A village in China from where Mao Tse-tung started his 'Long March'.
Set 6.explanation: Komagata Maru was a ship that sailed for Canada. In 1914, Indian businessman Baba Gurdit Singh hired it and set sail for the Canadian port of Vancouver with 376 passengers on board. After reaching the coast, the Canadian police surrounded the Indian passengers and prevented them from entering the country.

Set 6.q: 36. The Chishti Sufi order in India was established by
Set 6.explanation: The Chishti Sufi order was founded at Chisht (Chishti Sharif) in Afghanistan by ‘Abu Ishaq Shami’. However, in India, it was first propagated by ‘Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti’. He probably came to India in the 12th/13th century. He made Ajmer in Rajasthan his place of residence. He died in 1236 AD. Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki was his prominent disciple.

Set 6.q: 37. Which of the following poets was given the title 'Andhra Kavita Pitamaha' by Krishnadevaraya?
Set 6.explanation: Krishnadeva Raya gave Allasani Peddana the title of ‘Andhra Kavita Pitamaha’ or ‘Andhra Pitamaha’. He was a scholar of both Sanskrit and Telugu languages. He is regarded as the foremost among the Ashtadiggajas of Krishnadeva Raya. His major work is 'Svarochisha Manu Sambhavam'.

Set 6.q: 38. Why does dry HCl gas not change the colour of dry litmus paper?
options: HCl gas acts as a dehydrating agent.
Blue litmus dries up in the presence of dry HCl gas.
No H3O+ ions are present. Litmus changes colour only in the presence of H3O+ ions.
More than one of the above
Set 6.explanation: The colour of litmus paper changes in an acidic medium due to the presence of hydronium (H3 O+) ions. Dry HCl gas does not change the colour of dry blue litmus paper because it does not contain aqueous H⁺ ions. In this situation, neither is HCl gas in aqueous form nor is the litmus paper wet; therefore, the colour of the litmus paper will not change.

Set 6.q: 39. Assertion (A): A piece of ice makes a drink cold. Reason (R): Ice absorbs latent heat from the drink to melt, due to which the drink becomes cold.
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
Set 6.explanation: Heat is transferred from a hot body to a cold body. Ice starts melting by absorbing latent heat from the drink, while the drink becomes cold due to loss of heat. Both the assertion and the reason are correct, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

Set 6.q: 40. In the mains electric supply, a fuse is used as a safety device. Which one of the following statements about a fuse is correct?
options: It is connected in parallel with the main switch.
It is mainly made of a silver alloy.
It must have a low melting point.
It must have very high resistance.
Set 6.explanation: Fuse wire is made of a metal or alloy having a low melting point. Therefore, as soon as excess electric current flows through it, it becomes hot and melts. It is especially useful for the safety of electrical appliances. This is the heating effect of electric current.

Set 6.q: 41. In nature, which of the following organism(s) is/are most likely to be found alive on a soilless surface? 1. Fern 2. Lichen 3. Moss 4. Fungus (mushroom)
Set 6.explanation: Lichens are symbiotic associations of fungi and algae/ combines with the unsaturated bonds of vegetable oil and converts the oil into a more saturated and solid fat. This reaction is called the ‘hydrogenation’ of oil. Vegetable oil + Hydrogen → cyanobacteria. The fungi provide shelter, water and minerals to the algae, while the algae prepare food through photosynthesis. Therefore, lichens can grow even without soil on bare rocks, tree bark and other soil-free surfaces. Mosses are also non-flowering bryophyte plants, which do not have true roots; instead, they have rhizoids. In the presence of moisture and shade, mosses can grow on rocks, walls and tree bark.

Set 6.q: 42. When sunlight falls on raindrops, a rainbow is formed. Which of the following physical phenomena are responsible for this? 1. Dispersion 2. Refraction 3. Internal reflection
Set 6.explanation: A rainbow is formed by refraction, dispersion and internal reflection. When the Sun’s rays fall on raindrops, undergo two refractions and one reflection, a primary rainbow is formed. In a primary rainbow, the red colour is on the outer side and the violet colour is on the inner side.

Set 6.q: 43. The chemical used to destroy fungi in a water tank is—
Set 6.explanation: Copper sulphate is used to destroy fungi in a water tank. The hydrated form of copper sulphate is blue in colour; therefore, it is also used as a fungicide for the protection of crops.

Set 6.q: 44. Which one of the following statements about the amino acid tyrosine, present in protein-rich foods, is not correct?
options: It can help increase energy levels.
It can help cope with emotional and environmental stresses.
It can protect against free radicals responsible for ageing.
Set 6.explanation: Tyrosine is an amino acid from which important chemicals such as dopamine, noradrenaline and adrenaline are formed in the body. These chemicals are related to mood, alertness, attention and the ability to cope with stress. Therefore, tyrosine can help in maintaining mental alertness and energy. When there is a deficiency of tyrosine, a person may experience lethargy or sadness. However, the main function of tyrosine is not to protect against free radicals; this function is mainly performed by antioxidant substances. Therefore, the correct answer in this question is option (d).

Set 6.q: 45. Walking on ice is more difficult than walking on a road because—
options: Ice is harder than the road.
The road is harder than ice.
When we push with our foot, ice does not exert any reaction.
Ice has less friction than the road.
Set 6.explanation: We are able to walk easily on a road because the surface of the road is rough, due to which frictional force is produced. Because of its rough surface, we are able to place our feet firmly on it and push the Earth backwards, and according to Newton’s third law, we move forward. In contrast, walking on ice is more difficult than walking on a road because there is less friction on ice as compared to the road.

Set 6.q: 46. The gas used for making vanaspati ghee from vegetable oil is—
Set 6.explanation: Explanation: is Vanaspati ghee made from vegetable oil by the process of hydrogenation. In the presence of finely powdered nickel as a catalyst, hydrogen gas Vanaspati ghee

Set 6.q: 47. When the same note is played on a sitar and a flute, the difference between the sounds produced by them is due to a difference in—
Set 6.explanation: The quality of sound depends on factors such as the number of harmonics and overtones present in the sound and their relative prominence. When the same note is played on a sitar and a flute, the difference in the sound produced by them can be identified due to the quality of sound.

Set 6.q: 48. Which of the following is responsible for controlling hereditary traits in living cells?
Set 6.explanation: DNA is responsible for the control of hereditary characteristics in living cells. Genes are found in DNA, which perform the function of transferring and controlling characteristics from parents to offspring. RNA helps in protein synthesis, whereas enzymes and hormones control the biochemical and physiological activities of the body.

Set 6.q: 50. The layer of the Earth’s atmosphere called the ionosphere facilitates radio communication. Why? 1. The presence of ozone reflects radio waves towards the Earth. 2. The wavelength of radio waves is very long.
Set 6.explanation: Both statements given in the question are incorrect. Radio communication is facilitated due to the presence of electrically charged ions in the ionosphere.

Set 6.q: 51. Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
options: Formic acid – In the sting of an ant
Set 6.explanation: Citric acid and malic acid are mainly found in unripe mangoes. Tartaric acid, ascorbic acid and oxalic acid are also found in them in small quantities. Acetic acid is found in vinegar. The remaining pairs given in the question are correctly matched.

Set 6.q: 52. What is the chemical name of vitamin D?
Set 6.explanation: The chemical name of vitamin D is calciferol, the chemical name of vitamin C is ascorbic acid, and the chemical name of vitamin A is retinol.

Set 6.explanation: Crystallisation of sodium chloride and melting of ice are examples of physical changes. Sublimation is also an example of a physical change. Evaporation is also a physical change.
