Set 6.q: 54. The fuel used in a diesel engine is—
options: A mixture of diesel and petrol
A mixture of diesel, air and petrol
Set 6.explanation: A diesel engine is an internal combustion engine, which uses the heat produced by compressing air in a confined space to ignite the fuel. Unlike a petrol engine, a diesel engine does not have a carburettor for combustion. Therefore, the air inside the cylinder is compressed so much that the temperature of the air reaches 800°F or about 400–500°C. Due to the high temperature, diesel ignites spontaneously without a spark.

Set 6.q: 55. Which of the following statements is not related to nuclear fission?
options: Source of energy in a nuclear reactor that generates electricity
Production of a very large amount of energy in an atom bomb
Set 6.explanation: In nuclear fission, a ‘heavy’ nucleus breaks into two relatively lighter radioactive nuclei by absorbing a neutron or under the impact of a neutron. Their combined mass is less than the mass of the original nucleus, and this loss of mass is released in the form of energy. In contrast, in nuclear fusion, two or more ‘light’ nuclei fuse together to form a single nucleus, whose mass is less than the sum of the masses of the nuclei that fused together, and this loss of mass is released in the form of energy. The process of energy production in the Sun and other stars, and in the hydrogen bomb, is based on nuclear fusion, whereas the other three options mentioned above, namely (a), (c) and (d), are related to nuclear fission.

Set 6.q: 56. The Sir Creek dispute is between which two countries?
Set 6.explanation: Sir Creek, disputed between India and Pakistan, is an approximately 96 km long tidal/ marshy creek located in the Rann of Kutch. It separates Gujarat in India from the Sindh province of Pakistan. The main issue of the Sir Creek dispute is related to the demarcation of the land boundary in Sir Creek and the related international maritime boundary. At present, India retains control over this area.

Set 6.q: 57. India receives the maximum rainfall mainly from
Set 6.explanation: According to the data for the year 2024 presented by the India Meteorological Department, most of India’s total rainfall is received from the southwest monsoon. In the year 2024, India’s annual precipitation was recorded at 1206.6 mm, while rainfall during the southwest monsoon was 935.9 mm, which is 77.56% of the annual precipitation of 2024.

Set 6.q: 58. Generally, temperature decreases with increasing height from the Earth’s surface because: 1. The Earth’s surface is heated by absorbing insolation. 2. Humidity is higher in the upper atmosphere. 3. Air is less dense in the upper atmosphere.
Set 6.explanation: The Earth’s surface becomes heated by absorbing insolation. After this, the lower layers of the atmosphere are heated by terrestrial radiation, conduction and convection. Therefore, in the troposphere, temperature generally decreases with an increase in height. This is called the normal lapse rate, which is on average 6.5°C per 1000 metres. At higher altitudes, the air is less dense and water vapour also generally decreases. Humidity is not high in the upper atmosphere.

Set 6.q: 59. Which of the following is the first multipurpose river valley project of independent India?
Set 6.explanation: The first multipurpose river valley project of independent India is the Damodar Valley Project. The Damodar Valley Corporation came into existence on 7 July 1948. The Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) was conceived on the model of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) of the United States of America. It was constituted for the development of the Damodar Valley in the then Bihar and West Bengal. At present, its major area falls in Jharkhand and West Bengal.

Set 6.q: 60. Match List-I with List-II: A. Pampas B. Puszta C. Veld D. Downs | 1. Australia 2. South Africa 3. Argentina 4. Hungary
Set 6.explanation: The correct matching is as follows (Grasslands)  (Country) Pampas - Argentina Puszta - Hungary Veld - South Africa Downs - Australia

Set 6.q: 61. Consider the following statements— 1. The duration of the monsoon decreases from Southern India towards Northern India. 2. In the plains of Northern India, the amount of annual rainfall decreases from east to west.
Set 6.explanation: The duration of the monsoon is shorter in North India than in South India. The monsoon enters South India (Kerala) in the first week of June, while it takes more time to enter North India than South India. Similarly, during the withdrawal of the monsoon too, the monsoon winds retreat from North India earlier than from South India. In the plains of North India, annual rainfall decreases from east to west.

Set 6.q: 62. Match List-I with List-II: A. Birhor B. Bhutia C. Toda D. Sentinelese | 1. Andaman and Nicobar Islands 2. Tamil Nadu 3. Sikkim 4. Jharkhand
Set 6.explanation: The correct matching of List-I and List-II is as follows Birhor - Jharkhand Bhutia - Sikkim Toda - Tamil Nadu Sentinelese -  Andaman and Nicobar Islands

Set 6.q: 63. The names of four rivers are given below. In terms of length, what will be the descending order of these rivers, starting from the longest to the shortest? (i) Mahanadi (ii) Krishna (iii) Godavari (iv) Narmada
Set 6.explanation: The lengths of the given rivers are as follows River Length (in km) Godavari 1465 Krishna 1400 Narmada 1312 Mahanadi 851 Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

Set 6.q: 64. Which one of the following statements is not correct?
options: The Mahanadi originates from the Sihawa Hills.
The Godavari River originates in Maharashtra.
The Kaveri River originates in Andhra Pradesh.
The Tapti River originates in Madhya Pradesh.
Set 6.explanation: The Cauvery River is one of the historic rivers of India and is considered sacred by Hindus. It originates from the Brahmagiri Hills in the Western Ghats of Karnataka, which are located in Kodagu district. Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

Set 6.q: 65. The Tropic of Capricorn does not pass through
Set 6.explanation: The Tropic of Capricorn passes through the following countries/regions Brazil Australia Paraguay Madagascar Argentina Mozambique Chile South Africa French Polynesia Tonga (France) Botswana Namibia Hence, it is clear that the Tropic of Capricorn does not pass through Bolivia.

Set 6.q: 66. Palghat Gap is situated between which of the following?
Set 6.explanation: The Palghat Gap is located between the Nilgiri and Anaimalai Hills.

Set 6.q: 67. Which one of the following is a landlocked country?
Set 6.explanation: Hungary is a landlocked country bordered by Ukraine, Romania, Serbia, Croatia, Slovenia, Austria and Slovakia. Belgium has a coastline on the North Sea, while Romania borders the Black Sea and Ukraine borders the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov.

Set 6.q: 68. Match List-I with List-II: A. Kiel Canal B. Soo Canal C. Panama Canal D. Suez Canal | (i) The Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea (ii) The Elbe Estuary and the Baltic Sea (iii) The Atlantic Ocean and the Pacific Ocean (iv) Lake Superior and Lake Huron
Set 6.explanation: The Kiel Canal connects the Elbe estuary (North Sea) and the Baltic Sea; the Soo Canal connects Lake Superior and Lake Huron; the Panama Canal connects the Atlantic Ocean and the Pacific Ocean; and the Suez Canal connects the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea.

Set 6.q: 69. In the production of which of the following minerals does China not rank first in the world?
Set 6.explanation: According to World Mineral Production 2020–2024, in the year 2024, China ranked first in the production of coal, lead and iron ore, while Madagascar ranked first in the production of mica.

Set 6.q: 70. Consider the following pairs: 1. Mekong - Andaman Sea 2. Thames - Irish Sea 3. Volga - Caspian Sea 4. Zambezi - Indian Ocean. Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched?
Set 6.explanation: Explanation: River  Drains into Mekong - South China Sea Thames - North Sea Volga - Caspian Sea Zambezi - Indian Ocean

Set 6.explanation: The matching of the dams given in List-I with the rivers given in List-II is as follows (Dam) (River) Dulhasti Chenab Gandhi Sagar Chambal Ukai Tapi Tawa Tawa

Set 6.q: 72. The authority responsible for controlling government expenditure is—
Set 6.explanation: The authority to control government expenditure rests with the Ministry of Finance. The Ministry of Finance includes six departments – Department of Economic Affairs, Department of Expenditure, Department of Revenue, Department of Financial Services, Department of Investment and Public Asset Management, and Department of Public Enterprises. Among these departments, the Department of Expenditure is the nodal department for overseeing the public financial management system of the Central Government and matters related to the financial position of the States. Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

Set 6.q: 73. Who among the following was not a supporter of the idea of cooperative farming in India?
Set 6.explanation: Chaudhary Charan Singh was not a supporter of the idea of cooperative farming in India. He opposed Jawaharlal Nehru’s Soviet inspired system of cooperative farming. Therefore, the leader who is not considered a supporter of cooperative farming in India is Charan Singh. Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

Set 6.q: 74. The size of a marginal agricultural landholding in India is
Set 6.explanation: Operational holdings are classified on the basis of their size. According to the Agriculture Census 2015–16, the size of a marginal holding in India is less than 1 hectare. A holding of 1 to 2 hectares is called a small holding, 2 to 4 hectares a semi-medium holding, 4 to 10 hectares a medium holding, and 10 hectares or more a large holding. In India, the number of marginal holdings is the highest; in the Agriculture Census 2015–16, their share was about 68.5%.

Set 6.q: 75. Which Ministry/Ministries will implement the PM-SETU scheme? 1. Ministry of Labour and Employment 2. Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship 3. Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology 4. NITI Aayog
Set 6.explanation: The PM-SETU Scheme is related to making Industrial Training Institutes modern and industry oriented. It is implemented under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship. Therefore, only statement 2 is correct.

Set 6.q: 76. Consider the following liquid assets: 1. Demand deposits with banks 2. Time deposits with banks 3. Savings deposits with banks 4. Currency. The correct sequence of these assets in decreasing order of liquidity is—
Set 6.explanation: Liquidity means the ability of an asset to be used immediately as a means of payment or to be converted into cash. Currency is the most liquid, because it can be used directly for payment. Demand deposits come after currency, because they are payable on demand. Savings deposits have a withdrawal facility, but in the question they have been considered separately from demand deposits. Time deposits are linked to a fixed period, so their liquidity is the lowest. Hence, the correct order is currency, demand deposits, savings deposits and time deposits.

Set 6.q: 77. The apex institution in the field of industrial finance in India is—
Set 6.explanation: Explanation: The Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) was established as a financial institution on 1 July 1964 under the Industrial Development Bank of India Act, 1964. From the year 2004, it became a scheduled bank under the RBI Act, 1934. Since January 2019, it has been categorised as a private sector bank for regulatory purposes.

Set 6.q: 78. During which Five-Year Plan period was the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) established?
Set 6.explanation: The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development was established on 12 July 1982. This period falls under the Sixth Five-Year Plan period, 1980–85. NABARD is the apex development finance institution for agriculture and rural development and its headquarters is in Mumbai.

Set 6.q: 79. With reference to the unemployment rate and labour force participation, consider the following statements: 1. When the labour force participation rate increases, the unemployment rate decreases. 2. When monthly/quarterly labour market indicators are released...
Set 6.explanation: The Labour Force Participation Rate is the proportion of persons in the population who are employed or are seeking or available for work, whereas the unemployment rate is the proportion of unemployed persons in the labour force. Therefore, it is not necessary that the unemployment rate will automatically decrease when the Labour Force Participation Rate increases. If new persons join the labour force and do not get employment, the unemployment rate may also increase. The release of monthly and quarterly labour market indicators makes it possible to analyse separate trends for rural and urban areas. This makes it possible to understand fluctuations in unemployment in a more detailed manner. Therefore, only statement 2 is correct.

Set 6.q: 80. Consider the following statements with reference to service tax: (1) It is a direct tax. (2) It is an indirect tax. (3) It was implemented in 1994-95.
Set 6.explanation: Service tax was an indirect tax, which was introduced with effect from July 1, 1994, under the Finance Act, 1994. Therefore, statements (2) and (3) are correct, while statement (1) is incorrect. As per the updated position, service tax was subsumed into the Goods and Services Tax regime from July 1,

Set 6.q: 81. What is blue carbon?
options: Carbon captured by oceans and coastal ecosystems
Carbon stored in forest biomass and agricultural soil
Carbon contained in petroleum and natural gas
Set 6.explanation: The carbon captured by oceans and coastal ecosystems is called ‘Blue Carbon’. Mangroves, seagrasses and salt marshes found in these areas play an important role in carbon sequestration and form carbon sinks. It is noteworthy that these coastal ecosystems have a greater capacity to store carbon than forests.

Set 6.q: 82. With reference to lichens, which of the following statements is/are correct? (i) Lichens are indicators of air pollution. (ii) The study of lichens is called lichenology.
Set 6.explanation: Explanation: Lichens absorb pollutants from the atmosphere, and their presence/absence and diversity indicate air quality. Therefore, they are good indicators of air pollution. In places where air pollution, especially SO₂ pollution, is high, many species of lichens do not grow. The study of lichens is called lichenology. Hence, both the given statements are correct.

Set 6.q: 83. In an ecosystem, after energy is transferred from one trophic level to another trophic level, the amount of energy
Set 6.explanation: In an ecosystem, the flow of energy takes place from the abiotic system to the biotic system. According to the second law of thermodynamics, when energy is transferred from one trophic level to another, some of it is lost; that is, the amount of energy available decreases at every trophic level. Therefore, top consumers receive the least amount of energy.

Set 6.q: 84. Consider the following statements. 1. Biodiversity is generally higher at lower latitudes than at higher latitudes. 2. Along mountain gradients, biodiversity is generally higher at lower elevations than at higher elevations.
Set 6.explanation: An important rule of biodiversity is that it changes with latitude and altitude. Near the Equator, that is, in lower latitudes, the climate is comparatively warm and stable, and productivity is high. This region receives more solar energy and has had a longer time available for the evolution of species. Therefore, species diversity is generally found to be the highest in tropical regions. On this basis, statement 1 is correct. In mountainous regions also, biodiversity changes with altitude. Generally, at lower altitudes, the temperature is relatively favourable, more area is available and productivity is better. In contrast, at higher altitudes, the temperature is lower, conditions are harsher and vegetation may be comparatively sparse. Therefore, biodiversity is generally higher at lower altitudes than at higher altitudes. On this basis, statement 2 is also correct.

Set 6.q: 85. When was the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha formed?
Set 6.explanation: In Bihar, the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha was established in November 1929 on the occasion of the Sonepur Fair with the objective of organizing farmers and redressing their difficulties. Swami Sahajanand Saraswati was its first president.

Set 6.q: 86. The number of Indian states sharing a boundary with Bihar is
Set 6.explanation: The Indian states sharing borders with Bihar are Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and Jharkhand. Bihar also shares a border with Nepal.

Set 6.q: 87. ‘Jitwarpur village’, approved by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, is set to become Bihar’s first Shilpgram (Craft Village). This village is located in which district of Bihar?
Set 6.explanation: ‘Jitwarpur village’ is located in Madhubani district of Bihar. It is being developed as the first Shilpgram of Bihar. This village is a major centre of Mithila/ Madhubani painting and is known as the School of Mithila Painting.

Set 6.q: 88. As per the recent decision taken by the Bihar Cabinet, what has ‘Sanjay Gandhi Biological Park’ now officially been renamed?
Set 6.explanation: On April 29, 2026, the Bihar Council of Ministers approved renaming ‘Sanjay Gandhi Biological Park’ as ‘Patna Zoo’ and changing the name of its management society to ‘Patna Zoo Management and Development Society’. Set 6.q: 100. Which of the following is stated in the Constitution of India? 1. The President shall not be a member of either House of Parliament. 2. Parliament shall consist of the President and two Houses.
Set 6.explanation: Both statements are stated in the constitution. According to Article 59(1) the President shall not be a member of either Houses of Parliament. While according to Article 79, parliament shall consist of the President and two houses. Thus, in the Constitution of India, the President is a constituent part of Parliament, but the President is not a member of either House of Parliament. For this reason, both the statements given in this question are correct.

Set 6.q: 102. The Preamble to the Constitution of India—

is not a part of the Constitution and also has no legal effect

is a part of the Constitution, but has no legal effect independent of the other parts of the Constitution
Set 6.explanation: In Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973), a large Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court held that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution. The Supreme Court gave this decision by overruling its decision in In Re: Berubari Union (1960), which had held that the Preamble is not a part of the Constitution of India. Thus, although the Preamble is a part of the Constitution and may be used as an aid in interpreting other parts of the Constitution, it has no legal effect independently of the other parts of the Constitution.

Set 6.q: 103. Set 6.q: 139. Recently, in a historic judgment, the Supreme Court declared which subject as a ‘fundamental right’ of citizens under Article 21 (Right to Life) of the Indian Constitution?
options: Commuter safety and the right to safe passage on roads
Digital education in the mother tongue at the primary level

National Highways Authority of India and Others, the Supreme Court held that the safety of commuters is an integral aspect of the right to live with dignity under Article 21. A Bench of Justice J. K. Maheshwari and Justice Atul S. Chandurkar passed this order on 13 April 2026. The Court said that national highways constitute about 2% of India’s total road length but account for about 30% of deaths caused by road accidents. Issuing interim directions under Article 142, the Court emphasised measures such as preventing unauthorised parking of heavy/commercial vehicles on national highways, prohibiting the construction or operation of new dhabas/eateries/commercial structures within the Right of Way, removing unauthorised structures, operationalising the Advanced Traffic Management System (ATMS), patrolling, emergency medical response and improving accident blackspots.

Therefore, Parliament enacted provisions relating to the salary and conditions of service of the Comptroller and Auditor-General in the year 1971. Set 7.q: 6. Choose the correct statements from the following regarding the Directive Principles of State Policy— (i) They are inspired by the Constitution of Ireland. (ii) They are not enforceable by any court. (iii) The concept of a welfare state is not a part of them. (iv) Under these principles, the Uniform Civil Code is mentioned in Article 45.
Set 7.explanation: The Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution are inspired by the Constitution of Ireland. The Directive Principles are non-justiciable under Article 37. The Directive Principles are non-binding instructions given to the State for the establishment of a welfare state. The Uniform Civil Code is mentioned in Article 44. Therefore, statements (i) and (ii) are correct, while statements (iii) and (iv) are incorrect.

Set 7.q: 7. Consider the following statements: 1. In India, the Advocate-General of a State is appointed by the President of India on the recommendation of the Governor of the concerned State. 2. According to the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, at the State level, High Courts have original, appellate and advisory jurisdiction.
Set 7.explanation: According to Article 165(1) of the Constitution, the Advocate General of a State is appointed by the Governor of the State and not by the President. Therefore, statement 1 is incorrect. Advisory jurisdiction is exclusively granted to the Supreme Court of India under Article 143 of the Constitution.While High Courts do possess original, appellate, and supervisory jurisdictions, these foundational powers are derived primarily from the Constitution of India and historical Letters Patent, rather than the Code of Civil Procedure itself (which strictly regulates civil procedural rules).

Set 7.q: 10. With reference to the Union Government, consider the following statements: 1. The ministries/departments of the Government of India are created by the Prime Minister on the advice of the Cabinet Secretary. 2. Each ministry is allocated to a Minister by the President of India on the advice of the Prime Minister.
Set 7.explanation: The Cabinet Secretary is the head of the Cabinet Secretariat the and is also the ex-officio Chairman of Civil Services Board. His functions include providing information about the various activities of the ministries and the rules related to the conduct of business. Under the Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961, the ministries/departments of the Government are created by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister. A Minister is appointed by the President of India on the advice of the Prime Minister, and the allocation of ministries/departments is also made by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister. Therefore, statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

Set 7.q: 12. Select the constitutional bodies from the following and choose the correct option. (i) Comptroller and Auditor General of India (ii) National Human Rights Commission (iii) Central Vigilance Commission (iv) Finance Commission
Set 7.explanation: The National Human Rights Commission and the Central Vigilance Commission are statutory bodies. The Finance Commission is provided under Article 280, and provisions relating to the Comptroller and Auditor-General are contained in Articles 148 to 151 of the Constitution. Therefore, the Finance Commission and the Comptroller and Auditor-General are constitutional bodies. The National Human Rights Commission was established under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, and the Central Vigilance Commission was established under the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003. Therefore, the correct answer is option (d).

Set 7.q: 13. Which of the following statements regarding Parliament’s control over the Budget is not correct?
options: Parliament has no role in the preparation of the Budget.
Parliament has the power to increase the expenditure charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India.
Parliament does not have the power to impose any tax without the recommendation of the President.
Parliament does not have the power to increase any tax without the recommendation of the President.
Set 7.explanation: Expenditure charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India [Article 113(1)] is not submitted to Parliament for voting. These items of expenditure can be discussed in both Houses of Parliament, but their amount cannot be altered through voting during the budget/ appropriation process. Therefore, the statement that Parliament has the power to increase charged expenditure is not correct. Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

Set 7.q: 14. In which matter does the Rajya Sabha have powers equal to those of the Lok Sabha?
options: In the matter of creating new All-India Services
In the matter of amending the Constitution
In the matter of removing the Government
In the matter of moving cut motions
Set 7.explanation: The Rajya Sabha has powers equal to those of the Lok Sabha in the matter of amending the Constitution. Under Article 368, a Constitutional Amendment Bill may be introduced in either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha, but it must be passed separately by both Houses. Therefore, in this matter, the Rajya Sabha has the same power as the Lok Sabha. Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

Set 7.q: 15. Which one of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts states that the total number of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the Council of Ministers shall not exceed fifteen per cent of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha?
Set 7.explanation: By the Constitution (Ninety-first Amendment) Act, 2003, clause (1A) was added to Article 75 of the Constitution. It provided that the total number of ministers in the Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, shall not exceed 15 per cent of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

Set 7.q: 17. The principle of Anuvrata was propounded by—
Set 7.explanation: In Jainism, the Panch Mahavratas are prescribed– non-violence, truth, celibacy, non-stealing and non-pos session. In Jainism, for house holders, these Panch Mahavratas are practiced in the form of Anuvratas, because while living in the world, it is not possible to follow these great vows completely. Therefore, householders are instructed to observe these Anuvratas in a limited form. These five Anuvratas are— (1) Ahimsa Anuvrata, (2) Satya Anuvrata, (3) Asteya Anuvrata, (4) Brahmacharya Anuvrata and (5) Aparigraha Anuvrata. Nirjara. Samvara means stopping the inflow of new karma, while Nirjara means the destruction of previously accumulated karma. Penance, restraint, detachment and bodily austerity are considered helpful in Nirjara. In Jainism, the three bases of the path to moksha are the Triratna—right faith, right knowledge and right conduct. When the soul becomes completely free from karma, it is released from the cycle of birth and death and attains moksha. Therefore, all three given statements are in accordance with Jain principles.

Set 7.q: 18. Which of the following characterizes/characterize the people of the Indus Civilization? 1. They possessed great palaces and temples. 2. They worshipped both male and female deities. 3. They employed horse-drawn chariots in warfare.
options: None of the statements given above is correct.
Set 7.explanation: So far, no evidence of any temple or place of worship has been found in the excavations at Indus Valley sites. Therefore, the sources of information about the religious life of this civilization are figurines, seals, symbols used there and other remains. From these, it is known that the worship of Mother Goddess, Pashupati Shiva, linga and yoni, as well as the worship of trees such as the peepal and creatures such as snakes, was prevalent here. Among animals, depictions of the elephant, tiger, buffalo, rhinoceros and gharial have been found, but depictions of the horse are absent. Horse-related evidence in the Harappan Civilization is very limited and disputed. It is mentioned that horse bones and terracotta figurines of horses have been found at sites such as Lothal, Surkotada and Kalibangan, etc. Still, there is no evidence that horses were used to pull war chariots. Hence, option (b) is the appropriate answer.

Set 7.explanation: The basic objective of Jainism is to free the soul from the bondage of karma. In Jainism, karma is not merely a moral consequence, but is considered an extremely subtle material pudgala that binds to the soul. This karma covers the intrinsic qualities of the soul—knowledge, perception, bliss and power. Therefore, the destruction of karma is necessary for attaining moksha. In Jain philosophy, the concept of life is very broad. Life is accepted not only in humans, animals and plants, but also in one-sensed beings associated with stone, water, earth, fire and air. Set 7.q: 21. Which of the following statements is not correct regarding Balban?
options: He propounded the theory of Niyabat-i-Khudai.
He ended the influence of Turkan-i-Chahalgani.
Set 7.explanation: The real name of Balban was Baha-ud-Din. Nasiruddin Mahmud gave him the title of ‘Ulugh Khan’. He himself assumed the title of ‘Zil-i-Ilahi’. His reign was from 1266 to 1287 CE. Balban is famous for his ideas related to kingship. The nature and essence of his theory of kingship were inspired by Persian kingship. Balban described the king as Niyabat-i-Khudai, that is, the representative of God. After assuming power, Balban abolished the ‘Turkan-i-Chahalgani’ formed by Iltutmish. The major rebellion of Balban’s reign was led in 1279 CE by Tughril Khan, the governor of Bengal. Balban suppressed it and sentenced the rebels to death. The organized introduction of the Iqta system in India was not done by Balban, but by Iltutmish.

Set 7.q: 22. The first English-language newspaper published by Indians was—
Set 7.explanation: The first newspaper published in English by an Indian was Gangadhar Bhattacharya’s weekly ‘Bengal Gazette’. Among the given options, the ‘Hindu Patriot’ was the first newspaper published in English by Indians. It was published in 1853 CE. The first editor of this newspaper was Girish Chandra Ghosh (1853–55 CE). Harish Chandra Mukherjee (1855–61 CE) and Kristo Das Pal (1861–1884 CE) were also its editors. Surendranath Banerjee has mentioned in his book ‘A Nation in Making’ that he became the correspondent of this newspaper in London during 1874 75 CE and in Delhi in 1877 CE. Later, this newspaper was purchased by the British Indian Association. Thereafter, it began to represent the interests of landlords and moved away from national interests.

Set 7.q: 23. Which of the following statements is/are correct about the Vernacular Press Act? 1. It was enacted by Lord Lytton. 2. It came to be known as the ‘Gagging Act’. 3. This Act was repealed by Lord Ripon.
Set 7.explanation: The Vernacular Press Act was passed in 1878 CE during the tenure of Lord Lytton (1876 1880 CE). This Act was called the ‘Gagging Act’. Under this Act, cases were filed against some vernacular newspapers such as ‘Som Prakash’, ‘Bharat Mihir’, ‘Dhaka Prakash’, ‘Sahachar’, etc. Lord Ripon repealed the Vernacular Press Act, or the Native Language Press Act, 1878, in 1882 CE and established equality between vernacular newspapers and English-language newspapers.

Set 7.q: 24. Where is the famous Vijaya Vittala Temple, whose 56 carved pillars produce musical notes, located?
Set 7.explanation: The Vitthala Temple (Shri Vijaya Vitthala Temple) was built by the mighty king Krishnadeva Raya (1509–1529 AD) of the Tuluva dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire. The 56 carved pillars located in this temple produce musical notes. This temple was built at Hampi.

Set 7.q: 25. The annual session of the Muslim League in which Jinnah’s Two-Nation Theory was accepted was held—
Set 7.explanation: The historic Lahore Session of the Muslim League was held in March 1940. In this session, Muhammad Ali Jinnah, in his presidential address, prominently put forward the idea that Hindus and Muslims were not merely religious communities, but separate political and social units. On this basis, the Two-Nation Theory gained strength. On 23 March 1940, the Bengal leader A. K. Fazlul Huq presented the Lahore Resolution. In this resolution, the demand was made for independent states for the Muslim majority north-western and eastern regions. The original draft of the resolution is considered to be related to Sikandar Hayat Khan, but its final form emerged after amendments by the Subjects Committee. This resolution was accepted on 24 March 1940 and later became famous as the Pakistan Resolution. Therefore, the correct answer is Lahore.

Set 7.q: 26. The Sultan of Delhi who wrote his memoirs was—

Set 7.q: 27. Consider the following historical sites— 1. Ajanta Caves 2. Lepakshi Temple 3. Sanchi Stupa. Which of the above sites is/are also known for mural paintings?
Set 7.explanation: The evidence of mural painting is very clear in the Ajanta Caves and the Lepakshi Temple; however, the evidence of mural painting is not clear in the Sanchi Stupa. The toranas placed around the stupa are full of depictions of events from the life of Buddha and Jataka stories, and are decorated from bottom to top. Since the toranas cannot be considered a part of the stupa, option (b) will be the intended answer.

Set 7.q: 31. Who among the following was hanged by the British Government in the Kakori Conspiracy Case?
Set 7.explanation: In October 1924, Sachindranath Sanyal, Ram Prasad Bismil and others founded the revolutionary organization “Hindustan Republican Association” in Kanpur. On 9 August 1925, this organization looted the government treasury by committing a robbery on the “8 Down Saharanpur-Lucknow Passenger Train” at a place called Kakori in the Lucknow-Saharanpur division of the Northern Railway. This incident became famous as the Kakori Case, now known as the Kakori Train Action. In this case, 43 revolutionaries were arrested. Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Roshan Singh and Rajendra Lahiri were hanged, while Chandrashekhar Azad escaped. Therefore, he escaped from the Kakori Case trial. Finally, on 27 February 1931, he was martyred in a police encounter at Alfred Park in Allahabad, now Prayagraj, which is presently known as Shaheed Chandrashekhar Azad Park.

Set 7.q: 32. Which important event took place immediately before the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?

Set 7.q: 33. Which of the following Mughal emperors was crowned twice?
Set 7.explanation: The Mughal emperor Aurangzeb was crowned twice. His first coronation took place in Delhi on 21 July 1658. His second coronation took place on 5 June 1659, and he assumed the title ‘Abul Muzaffar Muhi-ud-Din Muhammad Aurangzeb Bahadur Alamgir Padshah Ghazi’.

Set 7.q: 34. By which of the following Acts was the system of communal representation introduced in British India?
Set 7.explanation: The Indian Councils Act, 1909, which is known as the Morley-Minto Reforms, brought an important change in the structure of electoral representation in British India. Under this system, separate electorates were introduced for Muslims, in which only Muslim voters participated in the election of Muslim representatives. Therefore, it is considered the first clear introduction of communal representation in British India.

Set 7.q: 36. Arrange the following Sena rulers of Bengal in ascending chronological order— 1. Ballal Sena 2. Lakshmana Sena 3. Hemanta Sena 4. Vijaya Sena

The first historically known ruler of the Sena dynasty was Vijaya Sena (1095–1158 AD), and he was the son of Hemanta Sena. After him, Ballala Sena (1158–1179 AD) and Lakshmana Sena (1179–1206 AD) became rulers of the Sena dynasty. The sequence of the rulers given in the question is: Hemanta Sena → Vijaya Sena → Ballala Sena → Lakshmana Sena.

Set 7.q: 38. With reference to Indian history, consider the following statements— 1. The first Mongol invasion of India took place during the reign of Jalaluddin Khalji. 2. During the reign of Alauddin Khalji, a Mongol invasion reached Delhi and besieged the city. 3. Muhammad bin Tughlaq temporarily lost some north-western parts of his kingdom to the Mongols.
Set 7.explanation: The first Mongol invasion of India did not take place during the time of Jalaluddin Khilji. The Mongol threat had appeared much earlier during the reign of Iltutmish, when the Mongols reached the Indus region while pursuing Jalaluddin Mangbarni. During the period of Alauddin Khilji, the Mongol invader Targhi/Taraghai attacked Delhi in around 1303 AD. At that time, Alauddin Khilji was engaged in the Chittor campaign. During the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq, a Mongol campaign took place under the leadership of Tarmashirin. However, Muhammad bin Tughlaq captured Kalanaur and Peshawar and foiled the Mongol campaign.

Set 7.q: 40. Which of the following Brahmana texts is related to the Rigveda?
Set 7.explanation: The Brahmana texts are prose texts related to the rituals, sacrificial procedures and their meanings/interpretations associated with the Vedas. The Aitareya Brahmana and the Kaushitaki/ Shankhayana Brahmana are related to the Rigveda. The Panchavimsha or Tandya Brahmana and the Jaiminiya Brahmana are related to the Samaveda. The Shatapatha Brahmana is related to the Shukla Yajurveda, while the Taittiriya Brahmana is related to the Krishna Yajurveda. The Gopatha Brahmana is the Brahmana text of the Atharvaveda. Therefore, among the given options, the Brahmana text related to the Rigveda is the Aitareya Brahmana.

Set 7.explanation: The correct matching of the organisations given in List-I with their founders given in List-II is as follows— List-I (Organisation)  - List-II (Founder) Landholders’ Society - Dwarkanath Tagore British India Society - William Adam Indian Society - Anand Mohan Bose Indian Association - S. N. Banerjee

Set 7.q: 42. Which medieval ruler of India introduced the ‘Iqta system’?
Set 7.explanation: Iltutmish is credited with giving an organised/ institutional form to the Iqta system in the Delhi Sultanate. Iqta was not a grant of land ownership; rather, it was a transferable assignment of the revenue income and administrative military responsibilities of a particular area. Its holder was called an Iqtadar, Muqti or Wali. He collected the prescribed taxes, used the revenue for his own salary and for the expenses of soldiers/ administration, and sent the surplus to the central treasury. He was also responsible for maintaining law and order and for providing military assistance to the Sultan when required.

Set 7.q: 43. Who was Alara Kalama?
options: A ruler during the time of the Buddha
Set 7.explanation: Explanation: After the Mahabhinishkramana, i.e., the Great Renunciation, in search of knowledge, Mahatma Buddha reached the hermitage of Alara Kalama and received initiation from him. He practised austerities in the hermitage of Alara Kalama, but he was not satisfied with it. Alara Kalama was a teacher of the Sankhya philosophy and was famous for his spiritual/meditative powers.

Set 7.q: 44. Who wrote the Mughal-period text ‘Maasir-i-Alamgiri’?
Set 7.explanation: The Mughal-period text ‘Maasir i-Alamgiri’ was written by Saqi Mustaid Khan. Written in the Persian language, this text provides details of the reign of Aurangzeb.

Set 7.q: 45. “If Muslims are happy and satisfied, they will be the greatest safeguard of British power in India.” Who wrote this statement?
Set 7.explanation: W. W. Hunter wrote in his book ‘The Indian Musalmans’ that “if the Muslims are happy and satisfied, it will be the greatest safeguard of British power in India.”

Set 7.q: 46. The Balkan Plan for the partition of India was the brainchild of—
Set 7.explanation: The Balkan Plan was Lord Mountbatten’s initial alternative plan related to the transfer of power and partition of India. Mountbatten assumed office as the last Viceroy of India in March 1947. After this, he held several discussions with Indian leaders. After 133 interviews between March 24 and May 6, 1947, he felt that the Cabinet Mission Plan was no longer workable. Against this background, he prepared an alternative plan, which came to be known as the Balkan Plan. Under this plan, provinces and some units could have been allowed to decide their own future. This created the danger of India being divided into many parts. For this reason, it was called the ‘Balkan Plan’, because ‘Balkanisation’ means the division of a large region into many small parts. Jawaharlal Nehru strongly opposed this plan. After this, it was abandoned, and finally, on the basis of the Mountbatten Plan of June 3, 1947, the process of transfer of power to India and Pakistan proceeded.

Set 7.q: 47. Cryogenic engines are used in—
Set 7.explanation: The word cryogenic is derived from the Greek word ‘kryos’, which means ice-cold, that is, cold like ice or low temperature. Generally, a temperature of -150°C or below is called cryogenic temperature. An engine that can easily use propellants stored at -150°C or below as fuel is called a ‘cryogenic engine’. Cryogenic engines are used in rocket technology.

Set 7.q: 48. Consider the following statements related to ionic compounds— 1. Ionic compounds are insoluble in alcohol. 2. In the solid state, ionic compounds are good conductors of electricity.
Set 7.explanation: Ionic compounds dissolve in water and dissociate into their cations and anions; therefore, their aqueous solutions conduct electricity. They are generally insoluble or only slightly soluble in organic solvents such as alcohol, because such solvents cannot dissociate ionic compounds as effectively as water. In the solid state, the ions of ionic compounds remain fixed at definite positions; therefore, they cannot move and do not conduct electricity. Hence, only statement 1 is correct.

Set 7.q: 49. Which microorganism is generally used in making bread?
Set 7.explanation: Yeast is generally used in making bread. Its scientific name is Saccharomyces cerevisiae. It produces carbon dioxide gas by fermenting the sugar present in the dough. This gas makes the dough rise, due to which bread becomes soft and spongy.

Set 7.q: 50. Which of the following is a plant hormone?
Set 7.explanation: Plant hormones are special organic compounds that are naturally produced in plants. After being transported, they reach different parts of the plant in very small quantities and influence and control growth and many metabolic activities. Auxin, gibberellin, cytokinin, abscisic acid and ethylene are the main examples of plant hormones.

Set 7.q: 51. An antigen is a substance that:
Set 7.explanation: Antigens are foreign or unfamiliar substances that, on entering the body, activate the immune system and stimulate the formation of antibodies. Antigens are generally found on the surface of bacteria, viruses, toxins or other foreign particles. In response to them, the body produces specific antibodies, which help fight them. Therefore, the main function of an antigen is to induce the formation of antibodies.

Set 7.q: 52. The term ‘Goldilocks Zone’ is often seen in the news in the context of which of the following?
options: The limits of the habitable zone above the Earth’s surface
The region inside the Earth where shale gas is available
The search for Earth-like planets in outer space
The search for meteorites containing valuable metals
Set 7.explanation: The Goldilocks zone is also called the habitable zone. It is a region around a star where suitable conditions exist for liquid water to be present on the surface of a planet. Liquid water is an important component in the search for life on planets. In our solar system, Earth is the planet located in the Goldilocks zone. Research is continuing in the search for other Earth-like planets. This zone is neither too hot nor too cold.

Set 7.q: 53. Ball bearings are used in bicycles and cars because—
options: The actual area of contact between the wheel and the axle increases.
The effective area of contact between the wheel and the axle increases.
The effective area of contact between the wheel and the axle decreases.
None of the above statements is correct.
Set 7.explanation: Ball bearings are used in bicycles and cars to reduce friction between the wheel and the axle. Ball bearings contain small spherical balls, which reduce direct rubbing between the axle and the wheel. As a result, sliding friction is converted into rolling friction. Since rolling friction is much less than sliding friction, the wheel rotates easily.

Set 7.q: 54. Which statement about red blood cells (RBCs) in humans is not true?
options: Normally, they do not have a nucleus.
They are formed in the bone marrow.
The spleen is called the graveyard of red blood cells (RBCs).
Set 7.explanation: In humans, the average lifespan of red blood cells (RBCs) is about 120 days. They do not have a nucleus. They are formed in the bone marrow and destroyed mainly in the spleen. Therefore, the spleen is called the “graveyard of red blood cells”.

Set 7.q: 55. Helium is preferred over hydrogen in gas-filled balloons because it—
options: Does not form an explosive mixture with air.
Set 7.explanation: Hydrogen is a highly flammable gas and reacts very explosively with oxygen in the air. The lifting power of helium in balloons is only about 92 percent of that of hydrogen, but helium is used in balloons because it is inert and non-flammable.

Set 7.q: 56. Sodium vapour lamps are generally used for street lighting because—
options: Their light is monochromatic and is not dispersed when it passes through water droplets.
They are soothing to the eyes.
Set 7.explanation: Sodium vapour lamps are generally used for street lighting because their light is monochromatic and does not undergo dispersion when passing through water droplets.

Set 7.q: 57. Common salt (NaCl) is formed from—
options: A weak acid and a weak base
A strong acid and a strong base
A weak acid and a strong base
A strong acid and a weak base
Set 7.explanation: The salt formed by the reaction between a strong acid and a strong base is called a “neutral salt”, such as NaCl and KNO3 .

Set 7.q: 58. The colour of an opaque object is due to the colour which it—
Set 7.explanation: When light rays fall on objects, they are reflected from them and reach our eyes, due to which we are able to see the objects. The reflected portion of light determines the colour of objects.

Set 7.q: 59. Match the following— A. Rhizome B. Stem tuber C. Bulb D. Corm | 1. Garlic 2. Elephant foot yam/Suran 3. Ginger 4. Potato
Set 7.explanation: The above matching is as follows: Rhizome : Ginger Stem tuber : Potato Bulb : Garlic Corm : Elephant-foot yam/Suran

Set 7.q: 60. Which of the following is the main component of cement?
Set 7.explanation:
Lime | CaO | 60 - 67 | Provides core strength; controls setting time and soundness.Limestone and silica clay are used as raw materials in the production of cement. When silica clay and limestone are heated together, they melt and react to form “cement clinker”. Gypsum, up to 2–3% by weight, is added to this clinker.
Silica | SiO2 | 17 - 25 | Imparts long-term strength and durability (dicalcium/tricalcium silicates).
Alumina | Al2O3 | 3 - 8 | Provides quick-setting properties; acts as a flux to lower kiln temperatures.
Iron Oxide | Fe2O3 | 0.5 - 6 | Imparts the distinct grey color; adds hardness and aids raw material fusion.
Magnesia | MgO | 0.1 - 4 | Adds strength and color in small amounts; excess causes unsoundness (expansion).
Sulphur Trioxide | SO3 | 1 - 3 | Retards setting time (typically added as gypsum) to maintain workability.
Alkalies | K2O, Na2O | 0.4 - 1.3 | Kept strictly low to prevent efflorescence (white staining) and structural reactions.

Set 7.q: 61. An artificial satellite revolving around the Earth does not fall to the Earth because the Earth’s attraction—
options: does not exist at that distance.
is neutralised by the attraction of the Moon.
provides the velocity required for its regular motion.
provides the acceleration required for its motion.
Set 7.explanation: Two types of forces act on an artificial satellite revolving around the Earth. One is the central force and the other is the perturbing force. The central force is the gravitational force of the spherical Earth, due to which the satellite obtains the required centripetal acceleration for its motion and revolves around the Earth in a circular or elliptical orbit and does not fall to Earth.

Set 7.q: 62. Which of the following are not tastes of the tongue? 1. Sweet 2. Bitter 3. Salty 4. Spicy 5. Umami 6. Sour 7. Pungent
Set 7.explanation: The five basic tastes recognized by the tongue are considered to be sweet, bitter, salty, sour and umami. These tastes are experienced by the taste buds present on the tongue. Spicy and pungent are not basic tastes; rather, they are sensations such as burning, heat or irritation, which are mainly related to nerve-related sensations. Therefore, among the given options, spicy and pungent are not basic tastes of the tongue. Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

Set 7.q: 63. Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
Set 7.explanation: The correct matching is as follows— Aluminium – Bauxite Copper – Cuprite Mercury Zinc Iron – Cinnabar– Calamine– Hematite Therefore, option (b) is not correctly matched.

Set 7.q: 64. ‘Budget’ is a document of—
options: The monetary policy of the government
The trade policy of the government
The fiscal policy of the government
The money-saving policy of the government
Set 7.explanation: The budget is the main document of the government’s fiscal policy. It gives details of the government’s estimated receipts and expenditure for each financial year, from 1 April to 31 March.

Set 7.q: 65. Consider the following statements: 1. Gross Domestic Product is the total value of final goods and services produced within the geographical boundary of a country in one year. 2. In Gross National Income, net factor income earned from abroad by the residents of the country is subtracted.
Set 7.explanation: Gross Domestic Product shows the total value of final goods and services produced within the domestic territory of a country in one year. Therefore, statement 1 is correct. In the calculation of Gross National Income, net factor income received from abroad is added to Gross Domestic Product; it is not subtracted. Therefore, statement 2 is incorrect. Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

Set 7.q: 66. With reference to NITI Aayog, consider the following statements— NITI Aayog was established on 1 January 2015 in place of the Planning Commission. 1. The Prime Minister of India is the Chairperson of NITI Aayog. 2. NITI Aayog is an apex policy think tank...
Set 7.explanation: The full name of NITI Aayog is National Institution for Transforming India. It was established on 1 January 2015 in place of the Planning Commission. The Prime Minister of India is the Chairperson of NITI Aayog. NITI Aayog is the main policy think tank of the Government of India, associated with cooperative federalism, policy advice and development strategy.

Set 7.q: 67. With reference to population density as per Census 2011, consider the following statements— 1. The population density of Uttar Pradesh was 829 persons per square kilometre. 2. According to Census 2011, Bihar had the highest population density among the states.
Set 7.explanation: Population density means the number of persons living per square kilometre in an area. According to the 2011 Census, the population density of Uttar Pradesh was 829 persons per square kilometre. Among the states, Bihar had the highest population density, which was 1,106 persons per square kilometre. Therefore, both statements are correct and the correct answer is option (c).

Set 7.q: 68. What is meant by venture capital?
options: Long-term start-up capital provided to new entrepreneurs
Funds provided to industries during losses
Funds provided for replacement and renovation of industries
Set 7.explanation: Venture capital is long-term start-up capital provided to new, emerging or early-stage enterprises. This capital is given for starting new businesses, promoting innovation or expanding a business. It is not short-term capital, a fund for making up losses, or a replacement and renewal fund.

Set 7.q: 69. What is the main function of India’s central bank, the Reserve Bank of India?
Set 7.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India is the central bank of India, and its main function is to determine the country’s monetary policy and manage the currency and credit system. It is also associated with regulating the banking system and supervising the payment system. The Reserve Bank of India was established on 1 April 1935 under the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

Set 7.q: 70. Disguised unemployment means—
options: Unemployment arising due to technological change
The marginal productivity of labour is zero
A large number of people remaining unemployed
Set 7.explanation: Disguised unemployment is a situation in which people appear to be employed, but their additional contribution to production is zero. If such extra workers are removed from work and total production does not decrease, it is called disguised unemployment. This type of unemployment is commonly found in the Indian agricultural sector. Therefore, the correct answer is option (c).

Set 7.q: 71. With reference to the deficit indicators of the Bihar Budget 2026–27, consider the following statements— 1. In 2026–27, the fiscal deficit is targeted at 3% of GSDP. 2. In 2026–27, the revenue surplus is estimated to be about ₹1,143 crore. 3. In the revised estimates for 2025–26, the fiscal deficit is estimated at 11.8% of GSDP.
Set 7.explanation: In the Bihar Budget 2026–27, the fiscal deficit has been targeted at 3% of the Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP). For the same year, the revenue surplus is estimated at about ₹1,143 crore. As per the revised estimates for 2025–26, the fiscal deficit is stated to be 11.8% of GSDP. Therefore, all three statements are correct and the correct answer is option (d).

Set 7.q: 72. What is the base year of the new series of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) in India?
Set 7.explanation: The Consumer Price Index measures changes in the prices of goods and services purchased by households at the retail level. In India, the base year of the new series of the Consumer Price Index is 2024 = 100. Earlier, the main CPI series was based on the base year 2012 = 100, but in the new series, the base year has been changed to 2024.

Set 7.q: 73. With reference to Goods and Services Tax (GST), consider the following statements— 1. Goods and Services Tax is a destination-based consumption tax... 2. Goods and Services Tax has a provision for Input Tax Credit (ITC)...
Set 7.explanation: The Goods and Services Tax is a destination-based consumption tax in which tax revenue generally accrues to the state or jurisdiction where the goods or services are finally consumed. Therefore, statement 1 is correct. The Goods and Services Tax has a provision for Input Tax Credit, under which tax paid at earlier stages can be adjusted against the tax liability at later stages. This reduces the problem of tax-on-tax. Therefore, statement 2 is also correct.

Set 7.q: 74. Match List–I (Finance Commission) with List–II (Chairman): A. 13th Finance Commission B. 14th Finance Commission C. 15th Finance Commission D. 16th Finance Commission | 1. Dr. Arvind Panagariya 2. Dr. Y. V. Reddy 3. Dr. Vijay L. Kelkar 4. Shri N. K. Singh
Set 7.explanation: Explanation: The Finance Commission is a constitutional body related to the distribution of financial resources between the Centre and the states. The Chairman of the 13th Finance Commission was Dr. Vijay L. Kelkar, the Chairman of the 14th Finance Commission was Dr. Y. V. Reddy, the Chairman of the 15th Finance Commission was Shri N. K. Singh, and the Chairman of the 16th Finance Commission is Dr. Arvind Panagariya. Therefore, the correct matching is A–3, B–2, C–4, D–1.

Set 7.q: 75. Which Ministry of the Government of India is concerned with India’s Foreign Trade Policy?
Set 7.explanation: India’s Foreign Trade Policy is related to the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. The Directorate General of Foreign Trade functions under this ministry. It is the key body connected with the formulation and implementation of the Foreign Trade Policy and export promotion.

Set 7.q: 76. With reference to External Commercial Borrowings (ECB) in India, which of the following statements is correct?
options: They are regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI).
They are regulated mainly under directions issued by the Reserve Bank of India and the framework of FEMA.
They are regulated only by the Ministry of Commerce.
They relate only to rupee loans taken from domestic banks.
Set 7.explanation: External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs) refer to commercial loans raised by Indian entities from foreign sources. In India, ECBs are regulated mainly under the directions of the Reserve Bank of India and the framework of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999. The Securities and Exchange Board of India is related to the securities market, while the Ministry of Commerce is related to foreign trade policy. ECBs are not related only to rupee loans taken from domestic banks.

Set 7.q: 77. Which one of the following is not a function of the Reserve Bank of India?
options: Acting as the apex institution for scheduled commercial banks
Set 7.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India is India’s central bank. It formulates monetary policy, controls credit, and works as the banker to scheduled banks and the regulator of the banking system. The work of credit creation is mainly done by commercial banks because they accept deposits and give loans, and credit expands through this process. Therefore, the correct answer is option (d).

Set 7.q: 78. The first Industrial Policy Resolution of independent India was announced in—
Set 7.explanation: The first Industrial Policy of independent India was announced on 6 April 1948. It is called the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1948. This policy accepted the role of both the public and private sectors; therefore, it is considered the policy foundation of the mixed economy in India. This announcement was associated with Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee, the then Minister for Industry and Supply.

Set 7.q: 79. Match the following plans and programmes— A. First Plan B. Second Plan C. Third Plan D. Fourth Plan E. Fifth Plan | 1. Rapid industrialisation 2. Community development 3. Expansion of basic industries 4. Minimum Needs Programme 5. Attainment of self-reliance and growth with stability
Set 7.explanation: Community Development was related to the First Five-Year Plan, rapid industrialization to the Second Plan, expansion of basic industries to the Third Plan, attainment of self reliance and growth with stability to the Fourth Plan, and the Minimum Needs Programme to the Fifth Plan. Therefore, the correct matching is A–2, B–1, C–3, D–5, E–4. Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

Set 7.q: 80. Match List–I (Deficit/Concept) with List–II (Most appropriate indicator): A. Fiscal Deficit B. Revenue Deficit C. Primary Deficit D. Total Debt of the Central Government | 1. Total outstanding liabilities of the government 2. Revenue expenditure − Revenue receipts 3. Fiscal deficit − Interest payments 4. Total expenditure − (Revenue receipts + non-debt capital receipts)
Set 7.explanation: Fiscal deficit shows the total borrowing requirement of the government, and it is calculated as: total expenditure − (revenue receipts + non-debt capital receipts). Revenue deficit is revenue expenditure − revenue receipts. Primary deficit is fiscal deficit − interest payments. The total debt of the Central Government shows the total outstanding liabilities or accumulated borrowings of the government. Therefore, the correct matching is A–4, B–2, C–3, D–1. Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

Set 7.q: 81. Who was a member of the Constituent Assembly of India from Bihar?
Set 7.explanation: Rajendra Prasad was a member of the Indian Constituent Assembly from Bihar. Later, he became the permanent President of the Constituent Assembly.

Set 7.q: 82. Under the e-Office mission of the Government of Bihar, which district of Bihar became the first to make the operations of its collectorate completely digital and paperless, thereby promoting good governance?
Set 7.explanation: Saharsa became Bihar’s first e-Collectorate/paperless Collectorate. Under the e-Office system, files and correspondence are processed digitally instead of through physical files. This makes it easier to track the movement of files, increases transparency and accountability, and speeds up work processes.

Set 7.q: 83. In the recently announced Padma Awards, three eminent personalities from Bihar have been honoured with the Padma Shri. Which of the following persons, who had served as a Vice-Chancellor, received this honour in the field of Science and Engineering?
Set 7.explanation: In the Padma Awards of the year 2026, Dr. Gopal Ji Trivedi from Bihar was conferred the Padma Shri posthumously. He received this honour for his outstanding contribution to agricultural science, agricultural extension, and agricultural education. He was a former Vice-Chancellor of Rajendra Agricultural University, Pusa.

Set 7.q: 84. Who highlighted the plight of the farmers of Champaran by writing under pseudonyms such as ‘Dukhi’, ‘Dukhi Atma’ and ‘Dukhi Hriday’?
Set 7.explanation: Peer Muhammad Moonis wrote, under pseudonyms such as ‘Dukhi’, ‘Dukhi Atma’, and ‘Dukhi Hridaya’, writings such as Champaran Mein Andher (13 March 1916), Champaran Ki Durdasha (10 April 1917), and Dukhi Hridaya (February 1917), and highlighted the plight of the peasants of Champaran. He also wrote articles on Mahatma Gandhi in Champaran, Hindu Muslim unity, etc.

Set 7.q: 85. Which of the following cities is located in the easternmost part of Bihar?
Set 7.explanation: Among the given options, the city located farthest east is Katihar. Bhagalpur is situated to the south-west of Katihar and Purnia to its north-west. Patna is located approximately in the central part of Bihar.

Set 7.q: 86. Whom did Iltutmish appoint as the first Subedar of Bihar?
Set 7.explanation: Iltutmish captured Bihar Sharif and Barh and defeated Husamuddin Iwaz Khalji near Teliagarhi in the Rajmahal hills. Iwaz accepted the authority of Iltutmish. Iltutmish appointed Malik Alauddin Jani as the governor of Bihar in place of Iwaz.

Set 7.q: 87. Who among the following was not a member of the Champaran Agrarian Enquiry Committee?
Set 7.explanation: The chairman of the Champaran Agrarian Enquiry Committee was F. G. Sly. Its members were L. C. Adami, Raja Harihar Prasad Narayan Singh, D. J. Reid, G. Rainy, and Mahatma Gandhi. M. E. L. Tanner was its secretary. Anugrah Narayan was not a member of this committee.

Set 7.q: 88. At the Bharat Electricity Summit 2026 held at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi, which state was selected as the Focus State Partner, where the state’s energy reforms were showcased under the ‘Powering Bihar’ initiative?
Set 7.explanation: The Bharat Electricity Summit 2026 was held from March 19 to 22, 2026, at Yashobhoomi, Dwarka, New Delhi. Bihar was included as the Focus State in this conference. The Bihar Pavilion was inaugurated by the then Energy Minister, Bijendra Prasad Yadav.

Set 7.q: 89. Where was the first session of the Indian National Congress in Bihar held?
Set 7.explanation: The first Congress session in Bihar was held in 1912 at Bankipore, Patna. This session was presided over by Raghunath Narasinha Mudholkar. The general secretary of this session was Sachchidananda Sinha, and Maulana Mazharul Haque was the chairman of the Reception Committee.

Set 7.q: 90. Who was the first Indian Governor of Bihar?
Set 7.explanation: Satyendra Prasanna Sinha was the first Indian Governor of the Province of Bihar and Orissa. His tenure was from December 29, 1920, to November 30, 1921. He is also known as ‘Lord Sinha’.

Set 7.q: 91. When was the attempt made to assassinate Kingsford in Muzaffarpur?
Set 7.explanation: On April 30, 1908, in Muzaffarpur, Bihar, Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki threw a bomb at a carriage with the aim of killing Kingsford. However, Kingsford survived, and unfortunately, the wife and daughter of Mr. Kennedy, who was sympathetic to the national movement, were killed. Prafulla Chaki committed suicide to evade the police, while Khudiram Bose was arrested and hanged.

Set 7.q: 92. Under the One District One Product scheme, the state’s first ‘Turmeric Cluster’ is being established in Sakra block of Muzaffarpur district in Bihar. Under this scheme, which famous premium turmeric variety of Meghalaya... will be cultivated?
Set 7.explanation: Bihar’s first ‘turmeric cluster’ is being developed in Sakra block of Muzaffarpur district, where Meghalaya’s famous ‘Lakadong turmeric’ will be cultivated. This variety is known for its high curcumin content of 7–12%, which is higher than that of common turmeric. Due to its medicinal properties, it is widely used in the spice, pharmaceutical, and nutraceutical industries.

Set 7.q: 93. Under the master plan prepared by the Water Resources Department, Government of Bihar, which pair is not correctly matched with regard to the digital database of dams/reservoirs and eco-tourism?
Set 7.explanation: Pair (d) is not correctly matched, because ‘Odhni Dam’ is located in Banka district, not in Nawada. Due to its natural beauty and facilities for picnics and water sports, Odhni Dam is included among Bihar’s developing water-based tourist destinations. Phulwaria Reservoir is located in Hardiya Panchayat of Rajauli block in Nawada district.

Set 7.q: 94. The Terai region of Bihar extends—
options: parallel to the northern edge of the Chota Nagpur Plateau
parallel to the eastern edge of the Rohtas Plateau
parallel to the western boundary of the Rajmahal Hills
Set 7.explanation: The Terai region of Bihar extends parallel to the India Nepal border. In Bihar, the Terai region extends as a narrow belt in the districts adjoining the Nepal border, namely West Champaran, East Champaran, Sitamarhi, Madhubani, Supaul, Araria, and Kishanganj.

Set 7.q: 95. Which one of the following reflects more insolation as compared to the other three?
options: Land covered with newly fallen snow
Set 7.explanation: The average albedo of the Earth is about 30%, while the highest albedo is that of land covered with freshly fallen snow, which is 80–90%. The albedo of sandy desert is 35%, the albedo of land under paddy cultivation is lower than that of land covered with freshly fallen snow, and the albedo of prairie land is 18–25%. Therefore, land covered with freshly fallen snow reflects the maximum amount of insolation.

Set 7.q: 96. Assertion (A): The frequency of landslides in the Himalayas has increased. Reason (R): In recent years, large-scale mining activities have taken place in the Himalayas.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
Set 7.explanation: Explanation: The Himalayas are one of the world’s young fold mountain ranges. Their rocks are relatively weak and brittle, and the slopes are very steep. In this region, the natural risk of landslides is already high due to heavy rainfall, cloudbursts, seismic activity, and river erosion. Human activities have further increased this natural vulnerability. Activities such as road construction, construction of dams and tunnels, deforestation, unplanned settlements, and mining and quarrying reduce the stability of mountain slopes. During mining, conditions such as rock cutting, blasting, accumulation of loose debris, and obstruction of drainage are created, which increase the possibility of landslides. Therefore, Statement (A) is correct that the frequency of landslides has increased in the Himalayas. Reason (R) is also correct, because large scale mining is an important human cause of the increase in landslides. Hence, (R) correctly explains (A), and option (a) is the correct answer.

Set 7.q: 97. Among the four southern states—Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu—which one shares borders with the largest number of Indian states?
Set 7.explanation: With the present state boundaries, among the four given states, Karnataka borders the highest number of Indian states. Karnataka shares borders with Maharashtra, Goa, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, and Kerala—a total of 6 states. In contrast, Andhra Pradesh shares borders with 5 states, Tamil Nadu with 3 states, and Kerala with 2 Indian states. Therefore, option (b) is the correct answer.

Set 7.q: 98. Rajasthan receives very little rainfall because—
options: the monsoon fails to reach this region
water is not available here and thus the winds remain dry
the winds do not encounter any kind of barrier, due to which they do not attain the height necessary for cooling
Set 7.explanation: Rajasthan receives very little rainfall. The main reason for low rainfall here is that the Arabian Sea branch of the southwest monsoon flows almost parallel to the Aravalli Range. Therefore, the Aravalli Range does not form an effective barrier to lift these moisture-laden winds. As a result, the winds do not cool and condense sufficiently, and rainfall remains low.

Set 7.q: 99. Consider the following countries— 1. Azerbaijan 2. Kyrgyzstan 3. Tajikistan 4. Turkmenistan 5. Uzbekistan. Which of the above share borders with Afghanistan?
Set 7.explanation: Afghanistan shares its borders with Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, China, India, Pakistan, and Iran. Therefore, it is clear that Afghanistan does not share a border with either Azerbaijan or Kyrgyzstan.

Set 7.q: 100. Consider the following statements— 1. The temperature range is high in equatorial regions. 2. In the Mediterranean region, rainfall is higher in summer. 3. Set 7.q: 105. Assertion (A): Mediterranean regions receive rainfall in winter. Reason (R): Westerly winds blow in these regions in winter.

Set 7.explanation: The Mediterranean type of climate develops due to the seasonal shifting of pressure and wind belts. In the Northern Hemisphere, during summer, because of the Sun’s northward position, all pressure belts shift northwards. As a result, the subtropical high-pressure belt extends over these regions, and anticyclonic conditions along with dry trade winds blowing from the land prevail there. Summer winds are generally dry. During winter in the Northern Hemisphere, when the Sun is in its southward position, the westerlies extend over these regions. Cyclones originating in the mid latitudes arrive along with these winds and cause rainfall. Moist westerlies and their associated fronts provide winter rainfall in the western coastal and windward areas. and his contribution to India’s economic recovery, especially to the assessment of a V-shaped recovery and policy discourse.

Set 7.q: 106. The Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ), a low-pressure belt, is located—
options: Between the belts of trade winds and westerlies
Between the belts of westerlies and polar winds
In the region near the poles
Set 7.explanation: The Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) is a low pressure belt found near the Earth’s equator. It is called a convergence zone because the northeast trade winds of the Northern Hemisphere and the southeast trade winds of the Southern Hemisphere meet in this region. Due to this convergence of winds, warm and moist air rises, which leads to the development of convective clouds, rainfall and thunderstorm activity.

Set 8.q: 3. Who among the following was the first European to initiate the policy of taking part in the disputes among Indian rulers with the objective of acquiring territory?
Set 8.explanation: The policy of gaining territory, wealth and political influence by taking sides in the internal disputes of Indian rulers is considered to have been started by Dupleix. Dupleix was a French officer and he took advantage of the succession struggles in the Carnatic and Hyderabad. He supported Chanda Sahib and Muzaffar Jang, and when they succeeded, the French obtained territorial and economic benefits. For this reason, he is considered the initiator of the policy of European intervention in Indian politics. Clive later adopted the same policy more successfully for British interests.

Set 8.q: 5. Find the correct chronological order of the Buddhist Councils held at the following four places: 1. Vaishali 2. Rajagriha 3. Kundalavana 4. Pataliputra
Set 8.explanation: The First Buddhist Council (483 B.C.) was held immediately after the death of Buddha during the reign of Ajatashatru, the ruler of Magadha, in the Saptaparni Cave at Rajagriha (Rajgir). The Second Buddhist Council (383 B.C.) was organized at Vaishali during the reign of Kalashoka, 100 years after the death of Buddha. The Third Buddhist Council (247 B.C.) was held at Pataliputra during the reign of Mauryan emperor Ashoka. Moggaliputta Tissa was its president. The Fourth Buddhist Council (1st century A.D.) was held at Kundalvana, Kashmir, during the reign of Kanishka. It was presided over by Vasumitra, while Ashvaghosha was its vice-president.

Set 8.q: 6. For which of the following rulers has the term ‘Eka Brahmana’ been used?
Set 8.explanation: The Satavahana ruler Gautamiputra Satakarni has been called ‘Eka Brahmana’ in the Nashik inscription of his mother Gautami Balashri, which means ‘a peerless Brahmin’.

Set 8.q: 7. The Treaty of Amritsar was concluded between Maharaja Ranjit Singh and .........
Set 8.explanation: On 25 April 1809, the Treaty of Amritsar was signed between Charles Metcalfe, on behalf of Lord Minto I, the then Governor General of Bengal, and Ranjit Singh.

Set 8.q: 8. Which of the following woman revolutionaries fired at the British Governor (Chancellor) while receiving her degree at the convocation ceremony?
Set 8.explanation: On 6 February 1932, Bina Das fired at the Governor from very close range while receiving her degree at the convocation ceremony of Calcutta University.

Set 8.q: 9. Which of the following denotes the tax levied on land produce? (i) Kharaj (ii) Khums (iii) Ushr (iv) Muqtai
Set 8.explanation: ‘Khums’ was not a tax imposed on land produce; rather, it was a secular tax. Khums was the booty obtained by looting the people of the enemy state during war. Of this booty, four-fifths was distributed among the soldiers and the remaining one-fifth was deposited in the royal treasury; but Alauddin Khalji and Muhammad bin Tughlaq kept four fifths in the royal treasury and distributed the remaining one-fifth among the soldiers. Except Khums, all other taxes refer to taxes imposed on land produce.

Set 8.q: 10. With reference to the Rowlatt Satyagraha, which of the following statements is/are correct? (1) The Rowlatt Act was based on the recommendation of the ‘Sedition Committee’. (2) In the Rowlatt Satyagraha, Gandhiji tried to use the Home Rule League. (3) The demonstrations against the arrival of the Simon Commission took place along with the Rowlatt Satyagraha.
Set 8.explanation: The Rowlatt Act was a black law under which any person could be arrested merely on the basis of suspicion. The Rowlatt Act was based on the recommendation of the Sedition Committee. This committee was formed to suppress revolutionary activities in India. In 1919, when Gandhiji appealed for Satyagraha against the Rowlatt Act, all those who had been made politically aware by the Home Rule Movement joined it. The Simon Commission reached India on 3 February 1928. In protest against it, strikes were held in all major cities and towns, and it was greeted with the slogan ‘Simon Go Back’.

Set 8.q: 12. When did Gandhiji give the slogan of ‘Swaraj within a year’?
Set 8.explanation: The Non-Cooperation Movement was formally launched on 1 August 1920. In the context of the Non-Cooperation Movement, Gandhiji gave the slogan of attaining ‘Swaraj within one year’.

Set 8.q: 15. Which one of the following is an example of rock-cut architecture?
Set 8.explanation: The Kailasa Temple of Ellora is considered a wonder of rock-cut architecture. This world-famous temple, built in the Dravidian style, was constructed by the Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna I.

Set 8.q: 16. Who conferred the title ‘Raja’ on Ram Mohan Roy?
options: Intellectuals who opposed the practice of sati
Set 8.explanation: Mughal emperor Akbar II sent Ram Mohan Roy as his envoy to the court of the then British King William IV in 1830 A.D., with the title of ‘Raja’. Roy was to negotiate in England with the King regarding an increase in the pension given to Mughal emperor Akbar II. Raja Ram Mohan Roy died on 27 September 1833 in Bristol, England, where his tomb is located.

Set 8.q: 18. Statement (A) : Ashoka annexed Kalinga to the Mauryan Empire. Reason (R) : Kalinga controlled the land and sea routes leading to South India.
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
Set 8.explanation: Ashoka conquered Kalinga eight years after his coronation and annexed it to the Mauryan Empire. For direct contact with the South, it was necessary for the Mauryas to control the sea and land routes. If Kalinga had remained an independent state, it could have obstructed trade through the sea and land routes. Therefore, it was necessary to annex Kalinga to the Magadha Empire. Thus, both the Assertion and the Reason are correct, and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.
