Set 9.explanation: The correct matching is as follows— (Doab) Bist Doab Bari Doab – (Rivers)– Between the Beas and the Sutlej– Between the Ravi and the Beas Rachna Doab – Between the Ravi and the Chenab Chaj Doab – Between the Chenab and the Jhelum

Set 9.q: 13. Which of the following seas has the highest average salinity?
Set 9.explanation: Among the options given in the question, the Dead Sea has the highest salinity, i.e. 238‰ or 238 ppt. It is a highly saline, closed-drainage water body. There is no outlet for water here, and due to intense evaporation in the dry climate, the concentration of salts increases. In the Black Sea, salinity remains low due to the fresh water brought by rivers. The Yellow Sea is also comparatively less saline, while the Mediterranean Sea has high salinity due to evaporation, but it is still much lower than that of the Dead Sea.

Set 9.q: 14. Match the following— A. Niagara Falls B. Land of a Thousand Lakes C. Eiffel Tower D. Roof of the World | 1. Pamir 2. Paris 3. Finland 4. United States of America
Set 9.explanation: Niagara Falls is located on the Niagara River in North America, on the border between Canada and the United States of America. Finland is called the Land of a Thousand Lakes. The Eiffel Tower is located in Paris. The Pamir Plateau is called the ‘Roof of the World’.

Set 9.q: 15. Match List-I (Mountain Passes) with List-II (States): A. Bum La B. Jelep La C. Muling La D. Shipki La | 1. Arunachal Pradesh 2. Himachal Pradesh 3. Sikkim 4. Uttarakhand
Set 9.explanation: The correct matching of the given mountain passes with their respective states is as follows— (Mountain Pass) – (State) Bum La Jelep La Muling La Shipki La – Arunachal Pradesh– Sikkim– Uttarakhand– Himachal Pradesh

Set 9.q: 16. Oxygen is absent from—
Set 9.explanation: Among the given options, oxygen is absent from kerosene. Chemically, kerosene is a mixture of hydrocarbons. It should be noted that hydrocarbons are compounds consisting only of carbon and hydrogen.

Set 9.q: 17. Which of the following rays/waves is used to monitor the development of the fetus in the womb?
Set 9.explanation: Ultrasound technology uses ultrasonic waves to examine the development of the foetus in the womb.

Set 9.q: 18. Pheromones are found in—
Set 9.explanation: Pheromones are chemical substances released by an organism to send signals to other organisms of its own species. Pheromones are observed especially in insects. They help in attracting the opposite sex, giving information about food or routes, warning of danger, and influencing behaviour.

Set 9.q: 19. A dentist’s mirror is—
Set 9.explanation: Dental specialists use concave mirrors. Large concave mirrors are used in reflecting telescopes to photograph celestial bodies, stars, etc. They are also used to examine the internal parts of the ear, nose and throat.

Set 9.q: 20. An alpha particle has a charge of +2; its mass is approximately equal to—
options: that of the nucleus of a helium atom
the sum of the masses of two positrons and two neutrons
that of two positrons, because each positron has only one unit of positive charge
Set 9.explanation: Alpha particles are made up of two protons and two neutrons, just like a helium nucleus. They are doubly positively charged helium ions. Their mass is equal to the mass of a helium nucleus. Their mass is about four times the mass of a hydrogen atom.

Set 9.q: 21. Which of the following has a negative charge?
Set 9.explanation: Alpha rays are made up of alpha particles, which are positively charged helium nuclei. Beta particles are negatively charged electrons, while gamma rays are uncharged. Gamma rays are electromagnetic waves.

Set 9.q: 22. Which of the following gases is found in the largest quantity in the atmosphere of Saturn?
Set 9.explanation: The atmosphere of Saturn is mainly composed of hydrogen and helium. Therefore, if it is generally asked which gas is present in the largest quantity in Saturn’s atmosphere, the answer will be hydrogen. But hydrogen and helium are not available in the given options. Therefore, after these, the more appropriate gas found in Saturn’s atmosphere is methane, whereas carbon monoxide, nitrogen and sulphur dioxide are not major options.

Set 9.q: 23. Assertion (A): Radio waves are bent in a magnetic field. Reason (R): Radio waves are electromagnetic in nature.
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
Set 9.explanation: Radio waves are electromagnetic waves and they do not carry any electric charge. Therefore, they do not bend or get deflected in a magnetic field like charged particles. Hence, statement (A) is incorrect. But reason (R) is correct, because radio waves are actually electromagnetic in nature. Therefore, the correct answer is option (d).

Set 9.q: 24. Which of the following is also used as a lubricant?
Set 9.explanation: Graphite is a pure crystalline allotrope of carbon. It is also used as a lubricant. In its crystal, carbon atoms are arranged in layers of regular hexagons. Due to the presence of weak van der Waals forces between these layers, graphite is soft and acts as a lubricant.

Set 9.q: 25. At absolute zero temperature, the electrical resistance of semiconductors becomes—
Set 9.explanation: At absolute zero temperature (0 K), the conductivity of a semiconductor becomes zero and it behaves like an ideal insulator. At this temperature, the electrical resistance of semiconductors becomes infinite.

Set 9.q: 26. ‘Plaster of Paris’ is made of—
Set 9.explanation: The chemical name of Plaster of Paris is calcium sulphate hemihydrate and its formula is CaSO4 ·½H2 O. It is prepared by heating gypsum [CaSO4 ·2H2 O] at a controlled temperature, due to which some of its water of crystallisation is removed. On adding water, it hardens again. Therefore, it is used for applying plaster casts to broken bones, making statues and preparing moulds.

Set 9.q: 27. Buckminsterfullerene is—
options: A form of carbon in which a cluster of 60 carbon atoms is joined together in a polyhedral structure made of pentagons and hexagons.
An isotope of carbon heavier than C-14.
Set 9.explanation: Buckminsterfullerene is a spherical fullerene molecule, which is an allotrope of carbon. Its formula is C60. In the structure of this compound, made up of 20 hexagons and 12 pentagons, carbon atoms are bonded in a polyhedral structure.

Set 9.q: 28. In winter, when the upper surface of a lake turns into ice, aquatic animals still survive because—
options: A sufficient amount of oxygen is stored in their bodies.
Their body structure is such that they can live even without oxygen.
The density of water is maximum at 4°C, due to which liquid water remains below the layer of ice.
Set 9.explanation: In winter, the upper layer of a lake cools below 4°C and eventually freezes at 0°C, but the water below remains in the liquid state at about 4°C. Thus, water remains below the ice in lakes or ponds at about 4°C, in which fish and other aquatic animals remain alive.

Set 9.q: 29. If the Earth’s gravitational force suddenly disappears, which of the following results would be correct?
options: The weight of the object would become zero, but its mass would remain the same.
The mass of the object would become zero, but its weight would remain the same.
Both the weight and mass of the object would become zero.
The mass of the object would increase.
Set 9.explanation: The weight of an object is the gravitational force acting on it. Its formula is W = mg, where m is mass and g is acceleration due to gravity. If the gravitational force of the Earth suddenly disappears, then g will become 0, so the weight of the object will become zero. But mass is the amount of matter present in an object and it does not depend on gravity. Therefore, the mass will remain the same. Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

Set 9.q: 30. Which of the following industries uses bauxite as the main raw material?
Set 9.explanation: Bauxite is the chief ore of aluminium. Its chemical formula is Al2 O3 ·2H2 O. In the aluminium industry, bauxite is used as the main raw material.

Set 9.q: 31. Consider the following minerals— 1. Calcium 2. Iron 3. Sodium. Which of the above minerals is/are required for muscle contraction in the human body?
Set 9.explanation: Calcium, sodium and iron are all important for the normal contraction and functioning of muscles in the human body. Calcium ions activate the process of muscle contraction, while sodium ions help in the conduction of nerve impulses and electrical signals in muscle cells. Iron does not directly initiate contraction, but it is an important component of haemoglobin and myoglobin, which help in supplying oxygen to muscles and in energy production.

Set 9.q: 32. Which of the following is not a nitrogen-fixing organism?
Set 9.explanation: Rhizobium, Azolla, blue-green algae, Nostoc, Anabaena, Azotobacter, etc. are nitrogen-fixing organisms, whereas mycorrhiza does not fix nitrogen. Mycorrhiza represents a symbiotic association between the roots of higher plants and fungi.

Set 9.q: 33. Red light is used in traffic signals because—
options: It is visible even to people with poor eyesight.
Set 9.explanation: Red colour has the longest wavelength, while violet colour has the shortest wavelength. Since scattering is inversely proportional to the fourth power of wavelength, i.e. scattering 1/λ, red colour is scattered the least and is seen most clearly from a distance. That is why red light is used in traffic signals.

Set 9.q: 34. Which of the following statements is false? A CPU cache—
options: is smaller and faster than main memory.
is used to store data from frequently used locations in main memory.
is accessed after main memory in read-write operations performed by the processor.
is used to reduce the time taken by the processor to access memory.
Set 9.explanation: CPU cache is used by a computer’s CPU to reduce the time and energy required to access data from the main memory. CPU cache is a small, high-speed memory that stores copies of data from frequently used locations in the main memory, so that the CPU can access them quickly.

Set 9.q: 35. Total Internal Reflection can occur when light travels—
Set 9.explanation: Total internal reflection can occur only when light travels from an optically denser medium to an optically rarer medium and the angle of incidence is greater than the critical angle. Diamond is an optically denser medium than glass. Therefore, when light travels from diamond to glass, total internal reflection may occur.

Set 9.q: 36. Match the following: (A) Plague (B) Filariasis (C) Beriberi (D) Typhoid | (1) Affects the intestines. (2) Spreads through flea bites. (3) Is transmitted by mosquitoes. (4) Is caused by deficiency of Vitamin B.
Set 9.explanation: The correct matching is as follows: Plague — is transmitted by flea bites. Filariasis — is transmitted by mosquitoes. Beriberi — is caused by a deficiency of vitamin B. Typhoid — affects the intestines.

Set 9.q: 37. Which of the following is a phosphatic biofertilizer?
Set 9.explanation: Rhizobium, blue green algae and Azolla all fix nitrogen, whereas vesicular arbuscular mycorrhiza increases phosphorus uptake and availability.

Set 9.q: 38. Which main mineral is used for making aluminium?
Set 9.explanation: Bauxite (Al2 O3 ·2H2 O) is the chief ore of aluminium, found as a hydrated oxide of aluminium. It consists mainly of gibbsite, boehmite and diaspore. It was first found at a place named ‘Les Baux’ in southern France. Therefore, it was named bauxite. Aluminium metal is mainly extracted from bauxite ore by electrolysis.

Set 9.q: 39. At the 21st Foundation Day of the ‘Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Authority’ held in New Delhi, which product of Bihar was honoured with the ‘Plant Genome Saviour Community Award’?
Set 9.explanation: Explanation: On the 21st Foundation Day of the ‘Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Authority’ held in New Delhi, the Mithilanchal Makhana Producers’ Association of Bihar was honoured with the ‘Plant Genome Saviour Community Award’. This honour was given for its contribution to the conservation of traditional agricultural biodiversity and local agricultural resources related to makhana.

Set 9.q: 40. Who opposed Mahatma Gandhi’s Champaran Satyagraha?
Set 9.explanation: N.G. Ranga had opposed Mahatma Gandhi’s Champaran Satyagraha. He was of the view that though the Champaran movement provided relief to farmers, it did not adequately raise basic economic issues such as excessive rent, debt and zamindari exploitation. Rabindranath Tagore gave Gandhiji the title ‘Mahatma’ during the Champaran Satyagraha.

Set 9.q: 41. The most prosperous and poorest districts of Bihar, respectively, are—
Set 9.explanation: The richest and poorest districts of Bihar are Patna and Sheohar, respectively. District level economic prosperity in Bihar is generally compared on the basis of per capita Gross District Domestic Product (GDDP)/per capita income.

Set 9.q: 42. The movement for a separate province of Bihar, which led to the announcement in 1911 and the formation of the new province of Bihar and Orissa in 1912, was led by—
Set 9.explanation: Mahesh Narayan died in 1907. He used to publish a periodical named ‘Bihar Times’. Through his newspaper, Mahesh Narayan raised the demand for the separation of Bihar. The separation movement began to gain momentum throughout Bihar. After Mahesh Narayan’s death, Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha became the leader of this movement. A demand was made to grant Bihar the status of a separate province from Bengal, which was accepted on December 12, 1911, at the Delhi Durbar held develop banking, insurance, IT and fintech services in an integrated complex. in Delhi. Brahmadev Narayan, Ali Imam, Mazharul Haque and Hasan Imam also joined Dr. Sinha. The Bihar Provincial Conference was organised in 1908–09. On April 1, 1912, a new Province of Bihar and Orissa came into existence, with Patna as its capital. On April 1, 1936, the Orissa Division was separated from Bihar and made a separate province.

Set 9.q: 43. Which statement is true with reference to ‘Chhoti Chiraiya’, the official mascot adopted by the Election Department, Bihar, for the voter awareness campaign?
options: It has been designed by Kripa Nath Jha of Madhubani.
Rahul Kumar, the artist from Nalanda who created this mascot, has been selected for the first prize.
The main objective of this mascot is to create awareness only among elderly voters.
It will be honoured on the occasion of the upcoming National Youth Day.
Set 9.explanation: The mascot ‘Chhoti Chiraiya’, adopted for the voter awareness campaign by the Office of the Chief Electoral Officer, Bihar, was designed by Rahul Kumar, an artist from Nalanda, who received the first prize. Its objective was to motivate all voters, including youth, women and first-time voters, to participate actively in the democratic process. Therefore, statement (b) is correct.

Set 9.q: 44. Which of the following National Parks/Wildlife Sanctuaries are located in Bihar? 1. Valmiki National Park 2. Dudhwa National Park 3. Gajner Wildlife Sanctuary 4. Bhimbandh Wildlife Sanctuary
Set 9.explanation: Valmiki National Park is located in West Champaran district of Bihar and Bhimbandh Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Munger district, whereas Dudhwa National Park is located in Uttar Pradesh and Gajner Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Rajasthan. Therefore, only 1 and 4 are located in Bihar.

Set 9.q: 45. Who led the peasants in Bihar during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
Set 9.explanation: Swami Vidyanand was a peasant leader of Bihar. During the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920–22), Swami Vidyanand led the peasants in Bihar. In several districts of North Bihar, particularly in the Darbhanga region, Swami Vidyanand was making raiyats aware of their rights.

Set 9.q: 46. Consider the following statements regarding the geographical and ecological context of ‘Gogabeel Lake’, declared India’s 94th Ramsar Site in November 2025— 1. This lake is located in the Trans-Ganga plain between the Ganga and Mahananda rivers in Katihar district of Bihar. 2. Gogabeel Lake is the first ‘Community Reserve’ of Bihar, which is conserved by the local people. 3. With the recognition of this new site, the total number of Ramsar Sites in Bihar has increased to six.
Set 9.explanation: In November 2025, Gogabeel Lake was designated as India’s 94th Ramsar site. It is a floodplain wetland located between the Ganga and Mahananda rivers in Katihar district of Bihar. It is also Bihar’s first community reserve, conserved by the local community. With its inclusion, the number of Ramsar sites in Bihar increased to six. Therefore, all three statements are correct.

Set 9.q: 47. In which mauza is the ‘Fintech City’, to be developed by the Bihar government at Fatuha in Patna district on the lines of Gujarat’s ‘GIFT City’, being constructed?
Set 9.explanation: The Bihar government is developing a ‘FinTech City’ on the model of Gujarat’s ‘GIFT City’ at Jaitiya Mauza in the Fatuha circle of Patna district. Approval has been given for the acquisition of about 242 acres of land for this purpose. The objective of this project is to

Set 9.q: 48. Yusuf Shah Chak, the last Muslim ruler of the Kashmir Valley, who was exiled to Bihar by Mughal Emperor Akbar, is buried in—
Set 9.explanation: Yusuf Shah Chak, the last independent ruler of the Kashmir Valley, was exiled by the Mughal emperor Akbar. During his exile, Yusuf Shah Chak died in 1592 CE in Puri (present-day Odisha). Later, he was buried in Nalanda district, Bihar.

Set 9.q: 49. Consider the legal and statistical grounds of the Special Intensive Revision conducted by the Election Commission of India in Bihar— 1. Under this process, the names of a total of 65.6 lakh voters have been removed from Bihar’s electoral roll. 2. Section 21(3) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 permits the Election Commission to conduct ‘SIR’ under special circumstances.
Set 9.explanation: During the ‘Special Intensive Revision’ (SIR) conducted by the Election Commission in Bihar, the names of about 65.6 lakh voters were removed from the list, including deceased voters, duplicate entries and voters who had permanently shifted. Also, Section 21(3) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 empowers the Election Commission to conduct a special revision of the electoral roll under special circumstances. Therefore, both statements are correct.

Set 9.q: 50. According to the December 2025 data of the ICAR-Directorate of Mushroom Research (DMR), Solan, Bihar has reached the first position with what percentage share in the country’s total mushroom production?
Set 9.explanation: According to the December 2025 data of the ICAR Directorate of Mushroom Research (DMR), Solan, Bihar reached the first position in the country, with about an 11 percent share in India’s total mushroom production. The state’s production was more than 41,000 tonnes. Schemes such as training, mushroom kits and subsidies for hut/ DPD units played an important role in increasing production.

Set 9.q: 51. The ‘Bihar Civil Courts Bill, 2026’, passed in the 2026 Budget Session of the Bihar Legislative Assembly, has replaced which nearly 139-year-old colonial law?
options: Bengal, Agra and Assam Civil Courts Act, 1887
Set 9.explanation: The ‘Bihar Civil Nyayalay (Court) Bill, 2026’, passed in the Budget Session of the Bihar Legislative Assembly, replaced the nearly 139-year-old colonial era Bengal, Agra and Assam Civil Courts Act, 1887. The new Bill modernises and streamlines the structure, jurisdiction and judicial system of civil courts.

Set 9.q: 52. From where did Vinoba Bhave start the Individual Satyagraha in 1940?
options: More than one of the above
Set 9.explanation: After the failure of the August Offer (1940), the Indian National Congress, under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi, started the ‘Individual Satyagraha’ on October 17, 1940. It was a non violent and limited movement whose objective was to protest against the British government’s decision to drag India into the Second World War without India’s consent and to assert the freedom of expression. This movement started from Pavnar Ashram in Maharashtra, and its first satyagrahi was Acharya Vinoba Bhave.

Set 9.q: 53. Which of the following prisons did Gandhiji call a ‘temple’?
Set 9.explanation: Therefore, the correct answer is option (a).

Set 9.q: 54. Which part of India remained under Portuguese control after 15 August 1947?
Set 9.explanation: Even after 15 August 1947, the Indian territories of Goa, Daman and Diu remained under Portuguese rule. Portuguese rule in Goa began in 1510 and ended on 19 December 1961 following India’s action under ‘Operation Vijay’.

Set 9.q: 55. When the Congress leaders condemned the Montagu-Chelmsford Report, many moderates left the party and formed which of the following parties?
Set 9.explanation: Explanation: The Montagu Chelmsford Report of 1918 was related to constitutional reforms in British India. The Congress considered these reforms inadequate and criticised them. In contrast, moderate leaders such as Surendranath Banerjea were in favour of accepting these reforms. For this reason, they left the Congress and formed the Indian National Liberal Federation. Therefore, option (d) is the correct answer.

Set 9.q: 56. In which city was the meeting of the Khilafat Committee held in 1920, which requested Gandhi to take over the leadership of the Non-Cooperation Movement?
Set 9.explanation: In 1920, Gandhiji advised the Khilafat Committee to launch the Non-Cooperation Movement against the British government. In June 1920, the Khilafat Committee accepted this advice at Allahabad (Prayagraj) and authorised Gandhiji to lead the movement. In September 1920, at the special session held in Calcutta and presided over by Lala Lajpat Rai, the proposal for the Non-Cooperation Movement was accepted.

Set 9.q: 57. Which of the following Sultans provided employment to the unemployed?
Set 9.explanation: Firoz Shah Tughlaq undertook some welfare measures for the benefit of the common people. He tried to solve the problem of unemployment by opening an employment office and, after thoroughly examining each person’s qualities and abilities, appointing as many people as possible.

Set 9.q: 58. The objective of the Butler Committee of 1927 was—
options: To impose censorship on national newspapers.
To improve relations between the Government of India and the princely states.
Set 9.explanation: The Butler Committee was constituted in 1927. It is also known as the ‘Indian States Committee’. Its objective was to examine the relationship between the Government of India and the Indian princely states and to make recommendations for improving the economic and financial relations between British India and the Indian States. The Indian rulers appointed the well-known lawyer Sir Leslie Scott to present their viewpoint before the Committee.

Set 9.q: 59. Consider the following statements about the Indian National Congress— 1. Sarojini Naidu was the first woman to become the President of Congress. 2. When C.R. Das served as the Congress President, he was in jail. 3. Allan Octavian Hume was the first British citizen who became the President of Congress. 4. Alfred Webb was the President of Congress in 1894.
Set 9.explanation: Annie Besant has the distinction of being the first woman President of the Indian National Congress. She presided over the Calcutta Session in 1917. A. O. Hume was the founder of the Indian National Congress, but he never became its President; he served only as its General Secretary. C. R. Das presided over the Gaya Session in

Set 9.q: 60. Match the following monuments with their related rulers: A. Double dome B. Octagonal tomb C. True-arched tomb D. Gol Gumbaz | i. Sher Shah ii. Muhammad Adil Shah iii. Balban iv. Sikandar Lodi
Set 9.explanation: Explanation: Monuments Double dome Rulers Sikandar Lodi Octagonal tomb Sher Shah True-arched tomb Balban Gol Gumbaz Muhammad Adil Shah

Set 9.q: 61. Who used the term ‘Sarvodaya’ for the first time?
Set 9.explanation: The word ‘Sarvodaya’ was first used by Mahatma Gandhi. Gandhiji wrote in his autobiography that he translated John Ruskin’s book Unto This Last into Gujarati and gave it the title ‘Sarvodaya’. Vinoba Bhave established the ‘Sarvodaya Samaj’ to propagate Gandhiji’s ideals.

Set 9.q: 62. How did the Nizam Shahi dynasty of Ahmednagar come to an end?
options: Ahmednagar was annexed to the Mughal Empire and Husain Shah was imprisoned for life.
The Mughal army destroyed Daulatabad Fort and killed Nizam-ul-Mulk of Ahmednagar.
Fateh Khan seized the throne of Nizam-ul-Mulk.
In 1631 A.D., Malik Ambar was defeated in a war with the Mughals and the entire royal family was killed by the Mughal army.
Set 9.explanation: During the reign of Shah Jahan, an attack was made on Ahmednagar in 1632 AD under the leadership of Mahabat Khan. To capture Daulatabad Fort, he won over Fateh Khan, the wazir of Ahmednagar, to his side. After a four-month siege, Daulatabad Fort was captured. Sultan Husain Nizam Shah III was taken prisoner and sent to Gwalior Fort, and Ahmednagar was annexed to the Mughal Empire.

Set 9.q: 63. The Harijan Sevak Sangh was established after the Poona Pact in 1932. Its president was—
Set 9.explanation: Harijan Sevak Sangh was an organisation associated with the Gandhian constructive programme, whose objective was the eradication of untouchability and the social uplift of the Depressed Classes. After the Poona Pact, this organisation was originally formed in 1932 as the ‘All-India Anti Untouchability League’, and later its name was changed to ‘Harijan Sevak Sangh’. Its first president was Ghanshyam Das Birla. Amritlal Thakkar was its secretary.

Set 9.q: 64. Who among the following started the Khilafat Movement? 1. Shaukat Ali 2. Muhammad Ali 3. Shariatullah 4. Abul Kalam Azad
Set 9.explanation: Explanation: The Khilafat Movement was a politico-religious movement in India, mainly led by Muslims. The objective of this movement was to put pressure on the British to restore the office of the Caliph in Turkey. The Khilafat Committee, formed to launch the Khilafat Movement, included Shaukat Ali, Muhammad Ali, Abul Kalam Azad, Hakim Ajmal Khan, Hasrat Mohani and Dr. Ansari. However, the credit for launching the Khilafat Movement is mainly given to the Ali brothers—Shaukat Ali and Muhammad Ali. Haji Shariatullah was the founder of the 19th-century Faraizi Movement.

Set 9.q: 65. Under whose leadership did the Sarabandi Movement of 1928 begin?
Set 9.explanation: Explanation: The Sarabandi Movement means a movement for refusing to pay tax or land revenue. Bardoli, located in Surat district of Gujarat, became a centre of political activity after 1928. The Mehta brothers of Bardoli, Kalyanji and Kunvarji, and Dayalji Desai launched a movement in support of the peasants in 1928. Later, it was led by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. Under Patel’s leadership, the No Tax (Sarabandi) Movement was launched in 1928.

Set 9.q: 66. Consider the following statements— Dadabhai Naoroji’s most effective contribution to the Indian National Movement was that— 1. He expressed the view that Britain was economically exploiting India. 2. He interpreted ancient Indian texts and awakened self-confidence among Indians. 3. He gave the greatest emphasis to the need for the removal of all social evils.
Set 9.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji was the first nationalist leader of modern India who, through deep research and analysis, proved that Britain was economically exploiting India and that a definite amount of wealth was being taken to England every year. In this context, he put forward his economic ‘Drain Theory’ and made it clear that India’s poverty was not natural but was the result of colonial economic policies and the flow of wealth from India to England.

Set 9.q: 67. What was the date on which the Muslim League observed ‘Pakistan Day’?
Set 9.explanation: The session of the Muslim League was held in Lahore from 22 to 24 March 1940. It was presided over by Muhammad Ali Jinnah. On 23 March 1940, at this session, a resolution was moved demanding autonomous and independent units for Muslim majority areas separate from India. This resolution later came to be known as the ‘Pakistan Resolution’. In memory of this date, ‘Pakistan Day’ was observed by the Muslim League on 23 March 1943.

Set 9.q: 68. In which one of the following inscriptions is Ashoka’s personal name mentioned?
Set 9.explanation: Ashoka’s personal name is mentioned in the Maski Minor Rock Edict. In most of Ashoka’s inscriptions, the ruler is addressed by titles such as ‘Devanampiya’ or ‘Priyadarshi’, but in the Maski inscription, his name appears as ‘Devanampiya Ashoka’.

Set 9.q: 69. Consider the following— The arrival of Babur into India led to the— 1. introduction of gunpowder in the subcontinent. 2. introduction of the arch and dome in the region’s architecture. 3. establishment of the Timurid dynasty in the region.
Set 9.explanation: Gunpowder had been used in the Indian subcontinent even before Babur’s invasion. However, the credit for using cannons and guns in India is given to Babur. The blood of two valiant lineages of Asia flowed in the veins of Zahir ud-din Muhammad Babur. From his mother’s side, he was a descendant of Genghis Khan (Mongol), and from his father’s side, he was a descendant of Timur. Therefore, with Babur’s accession to power, the Timurid dynasty was established in this region. Timur believed in the divine element of sovereignty as well as in the indivisible authority of the sovereign. The construction of arches and domes had already begun in the Sultanate period. Therefore, option (b) is the correct answer.

Set 9.q: 70. Match the following correctly— A. Afonso de Albuquerque B. Nuno da Cunha C. Pedro Álvares Cabral D. Francisco de Almeida | (i) Shifting of the Portuguese headquarters from Cochin to Goa (ii) Arrival in India in September, 1500 (iii) Blue Water Policy (iv) Acquisition of Goa in 1510
Set 9.explanation: Alfonso de Albuquerque invaded Goa in 1510 AD and captured it. Nuno da Cunha shifted the Portuguese headquarters from Cochin to Goa in 1530 AD. Pedro Álvares Cabral arrived in India in September 1500. In 1505 AD, Francisco de Almeida was appointed the first Portuguese Governor and Viceroy in India. His policies were known as the ‘Blue Water Policy’ because their main objective was to establish dominance in the Indian Ocean region.

Set 9.q: 71. The radical wing of the Congress Party, with Jawaharlal Nehru as one of its main leaders, founded the ‘Independence for India League’ in opposition to:
Set 9.explanation: Under the leadership of Jawaharlal Nehru, young and radical nationalists objected to the ‘Nehru Report’. They were demanding that complete independence should be made the immediate goal. As a result, Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhas Chandra Bose formed a pressure group within the Congress in the form of the ‘Independence for India League’.

Set 9.q: 72. Under British rule in India, who is considered the father of dyarchy?
Set 9.explanation: Sir Lionel Curtis is considered the father of dyarchy. His ideas related to dyarchy became the basis of the ‘Government of India Act, 1919’. Under this system, provincial administration was divided into two parts—reserved subjects and transferred subjects.

Set 9.q: 73. Which of the following Sikh Gurus were executed by the contemporary rulers? 1. Guru Angad 2. Guru Arjan Dev 3. Guru Hargobind 4. Guru Tegh Bahadur
Set 9.explanation: 29 metres, which he had set at the Hangzhou 2022 Asian Para Games. Sumit Antil has won gold medals in the javelin throw F64 event at the Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024 Paralympic Games.

Set 9.q: 74. Who presided over the first session of the All India Kisan Sabha?
Set 9.explanation: In April 1936, the ‘All India Kisan Congress’ was established in Lucknow, whose name was later changed to the ‘All India Kisan Sabha’. Swami Sahajanand Saraswati, the founder of the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha, became its first president, and N.G. Ranga, a leader of the peasant movement in Andhra and a scholar of agrarian problems, was elected its general secretary.

Set 9.q: 75. The names of the 16 Janapadas of the Mahajanapada age are generally found mentioned in Buddhist literature. Which of the following Janapadas are mentioned in Panini’s Ashtadhyayi? A. Magadha B. Ashmaka C. Kamboja D. Chedi E. Vatsa
Set 9.explanation: Panini was the greatest grammarian of the Sanskrit language. He was born in Gandhara, located in the then north-western part of India. His grammatical work is called the Ashtadhyayi. The Ashtadhyayi has eight chapters and about 4000 sutras. The major Janapadas mentioned in the sutra text of Panini’s Ashtadhyayi are— Magadha, Ashmaka, Kamboja, Gandhara, Shurasena, etc. The list of 16 Mahajanapadas is found in the Buddhist text Anguttara Nikaya and the Jain text Bhagavati Sutra.

Set 9.q: 76. Identify the first ruler of Vijayanagara who captured Goa from the Bahmanis.
Set 9.explanation: After the death of Bukka I in 1377 AD, his son Harihara II ascended the throne. He assumed the title of ‘Maharajadhiraja’. He conquered regions such as Kanara, Mysore, Trichinopoly and Kanchi, and collected revenue from the king of Sri Lanka. He also had conflicts with the Bahmani kingdom. Harihara II’s greatest success was capturing Belgaum and Goa from the Bahmani kingdom in the west. He was a devotee of Shiva in the form of Virupaksha.

Set 9.q: 77. Consider the following statements— 1. Kitab-i-Nauras, a collection of songs in praise of Hindu deities and Muslim saints, was written by Ibrahim Adil Shah II. 2. Amir Khusrau was the originator in India of the early form of the musical style known as Qawwali.
Set 9.explanation: In Kitab-i-Nauras, along with Hindu deities such as Saraswati and Ganesha, sentiments related to the Prophet of Islam and the Sufi saint Gesu Daraz are also found. Ibrahim Adil Shah II, the Sultan of Bijapur, composed the collection of songs called Kitab-i Nauras. He also founded the city of ‘Nauraspur’ and made it his capital. Amir Khusrau was the initiator of the early form of the musical style called Qawwali in India.

Set 9.q: 78. Match the following— A. Prarthana Samaj B. Ramakrishna Mission C. Satyashodhak Samaj D. Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College | 1. Swami Vivekananda 2. Mahadev Govind Ranade 3. Sir Syed Ahmad Khan 4. Jyotiba Phule
Set 9.explanation: Prarthana Samaj was established in Bombay in 1867 AD by Dr. Atmaram Pandurang under the inspiration of Keshab Chandra Sen. Mahadev Govind Ranade joined this institution in 1869 AD. Ramakrishna Mission was established by Swami Vivekananda in 1897 AD. Satyashodhak Samaj was established by Jyotiba Phule in 1873 AD. The Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College, Aligarh, was established by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan.

Set 9.q: 79. The Mahajanapada situated on the bank of the Godavari River was—
Set 9.explanation: According to the Buddhist text Anguttara Nikaya, among the 16 Mahajanapadas described in the 6th century BC, Assaka or Ashmaka was situated between the Narmada and Godavari rivers. Its capital was Paithan, whose ancient name was Pratishthana, or Potana or Potali.

At the time of the Calcutta riots
At the time of the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre
At the time of the Delhi riots

Set 9.explanation: Bal Gangadhar Tilak was politically an extremist leader, but on social issues, he had deep faith in conservative ideas. He supported political measures such as Swaraj, Swadeshi, boycott and national education. Therefore, he is placed in the extremist stream. On the question of social reforms, he opposed interference by British rule and believed that social change should develop from within Indian society. He developed nationalist sentiment through traditional Hindu symbols such as the ‘Ganapati Utsav’ and the ‘Shivaji Utsav’.

Set 9.q: 84. Consider the following texts and arrange them in chronological order— 1. Fatawa-i-Jahandari 2. Prithviraja-Raso 3. Kitab-ul-Hind 4. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri
Set 9.explanation: The author of the book ‘Fatawa-i-Jahandari’ is Ziauddin Barani. ‘Prithviraj Raso’ was written by Chand Bardai, ‘Kitab-ul-Hind’ was composed by Al-Biruni, and ‘Tabaqat-i-Nasiri’ is the work of Minhaj-us-Siraj, which he dedicated to the Mamluk Sultan Nasiruddin Mahmud. Therefore, their correct chronological order is—Kitab-ul Hind, Prithviraj Raso, Tabaqat-i Nasiri, Fatawa-i-Jahandari.

Set 9.q: 85. Which treaty was signed after the Battle of Buxar?
Set 9.explanation: The Battle of Buxar, fought in October 1764, was fought between the combined forces of Mir Qasim, the Nawab of Awadh Shuja ud-Daulah and the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II on one side, and the British on the other. The British won the battle. The British army was led by Hector Munro. After this battle, two Treaties of Allahabad were signed in 1765 AD. The First Treaty of Allahabad was signed between Clive and the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II, while the Second Treaty of Allahabad was signed between Clive and the Nawab of Awadh Shuja-ud Daulah.

Set 9.q: 86. The ‘Father of the Green Revolution’ in the world is—
Set 9.explanation: Globally, Norman E. Borlaug is considered the Father of the Green Revolution. He played an important role in spreading high yielding wheat varieties and modern agricultural techniques. He was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in

Set 9.q: 87. Which of the following statements is/are correct with reference to the ‘Make in India’ programme? 1. The ‘Make in India’ programme was launched in the year 2014. 2. Its objective is to encourage companies to manufacture in India and to facilitate investment.
Set 9.explanation: The ‘Make in India’ programme was launched on 25 September 2014. Its objective is to facilitate investment in India, promote innovation, strengthen infrastructure and make India a major hub of manufacturing, design and innovation. Therefore, both statements are correct and the correct answer is option (a).

Set 9.q: 88. Who introduced income tax in India?
Set 9.explanation: The beginning of the modern income tax system in India is associated with James Wilson. In July 1860, a bill imposing tax on profits arising from property, professions, trades and offices in India received the assent of the Governor-General. This is considered the initial basis of modern income tax law. Therefore, the correct answer is option (c).

Set 9.q: 90. What is meant by ‘blue-chip securities’?
options: Shares listed on the stock exchange.
Shares which continuously yield a high rate of return.
Set 9.explanation: Blue-chip securities refer to the shares of large and strong companies that have a good reputation in the market. Such companies generally provide stable earnings and good dividends over a long period. These shares do not have a government guarantee, and merely being listed on a stock exchange does not make them blue-chip securities. Therefore, the correct answer is option (c).

Set 9.q: 91. What does ‘paper gold’ mean?
options: Special Drawing Rights of the International Monetary Fund
Special Assistance Facility of the World Bank
Currencies which are still on the gold standard
Set 9.explanation: ‘Paper Gold’ refers to the Special Drawing Rights of the International Monetary Fund. In English, it is called Special Drawing Rights. The IMF created it in 1969 to supplement the official foreign exchange reserves of member countries. Initially, its value was linked to a fixed quantity of gold; therefore, it was called “Paper Gold”.

Set 9.explanation: The Training of Rural Youth for Self-Employment Programme started in 1979. After this, the Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas Programme started in 1982–83. The Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana was implemented in 1999

Set 9.explanation: Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin was launched in 2016, PM-KISAN Samman Nidhi in February 2019, Jal Jeevan Mission on 15 August 2019, and Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana in

Set 9.q: 94. With reference to the Gini coefficient, which of the following statements is/are correct? I. It measures the level of income inequality in society. II. The higher the Gini coefficient, the lower the inequality. III. It is derived using the Lorenz curve.
Set 9.explanation: The Gini coefficient is a mathematical indicator used to measure inequality in the distribution of income or consumption expenditure. It was propounded by Corrado Gini. It is calculated on the basis of the area between the Lorenz curve and the line of perfect equality. Therefore, statements I and III are correct. When the value of the Gini coefficient is 0, it indicates perfect equality, and when it is 1, it indicates perfect inequality. Therefore, the higher the Gini coefficient, the higher the inequality, not lower. Hence, statement II is incorrect and the correct answer is option (b).

Set 9.q: 95. Which of the following organisations publishes the ‘World Economic Outlook’?
Set 9.explanation: The ‘World Economic Outlook’ is published by the International Monetary Fund. This report presents assessments related to the state of the world economy, growth rates, risks and economic policies. The United Nations Development Programme is associated with the Human Development Report, the World Economic Forum with the Global Competitiveness Report, and the World Bank with the World Development Report.

Set 9.q: 96. Match List-I and List-II: A. Rule of Law B. Procedure established by law C. Reservation of a Bill by the Governor... D. Detailed Concurrent List | 1. Australia 2. Great Britain 3. Japan 4. Canada

Set 9.q: 97. In the context of India, which of the following is the correct relationship between rights and duties?
options: Rights are individual; therefore, they are independent of society and duties.
For the development of a citizen’s personality, rights, not duties, are important.
For the stability of the State, duties, not rights, are important.
Set 9.explanation: In the context of India, rights and duties are two aspects of the same thing. Rights are important for the development of human personality. They provide an individual with sufficient scope to act freely and thus create the basis for self-development. Although rights have special importance in a democratic system, they become meaningless in the absence of duties. If a person has rights, they should contribute to good work. A person does not have the right to perform anti-social acts. The rights of an individual show the individual’s claims on society, whereas duties indicate the claims of society on the individual. Therefore, in the context of India, rights are co-related with duties.

Set 9.q: 98. With reference to the Central Government, consider the following statements: 1. On 15 August 1947, the number of ministries at the Centre was 18. 2. At present, the number of ministries at the Centre is 36.
Set 9.explanation: The number of ministries in the Central Government is not a fixed constitutional number. It may change according to the allocation of work in the government, administrative requirements, and the creation or reorganization of ministries. On 15 August 1947, the number of ministries at the Centre was 18. At present, apart from the Prime Minister’s Office, the total number of ministries at the Centre is

Set 9.q: 99. In the context of India, which of the following principles is/are institutionally embodied in the parliamentary system of government? 1. The members of the Cabinet are members of Parliament. 2. Ministers remain in office only as long as they enjoy the confidence of Parliament. 3. The Head of State is the Head of the Cabinet.
Set 9.explanation: Article 75(5) provides that a Minister who is not a member of either House of Parliament for any period of six consecutive months shall cease to be a Minister at the expiration of that period. This means that the members of the Council of Ministers are to be members of Parliament. The Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha [Article 75(3)]. Therefore, statement 2 is also correct, because the Lok Sabha is a part of Parliament. In India, the head of the State is the President, whereas the Cabinet is headed by the Prime Minister. Therefore, the correct answer is option (a).

Set 9.q: 100. With reference to the election of the President of India, consider the following statements— 1. The value of the vote of each MLA differs from State to State. 2. The value of the vote of members of the Lok Sabha is greater than the value of the vote of members of the Rajya Sabha.
Set 9.explanation: Explanation: According to the manner of election of the President given in Article 55 of the Constitution, the President is elected in accordance with the “system of proportional representation” by means of the single transferable vote. The elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States and the elected members of both Houses of Parliament participate in this election. The value of the vote of each member of a State Legislative Assembly is calculated by the following formula— Value of vote of each MLA = Population of the State / Total number of elected members of the State Legislative Assembly × 1/1000 As the population of each State and the total number of elected members vary from State to State, the value of the vote of each MLA also varies from State to State. Thus, statement (1) is correct. The following formula is used to calculate the value of the vote of a Member of Parliament— Value of vote of each MP = Total value of votes of all elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies / Total number of elected members of both Houses of Parliament Therefore, it is clear that the value of the vote of each member of the Lok Sabha and each member of the Rajya Sabha is the same. If the vote value of one member is calculated, the vote value of each member of both Houses is equal. In the 16th Presidential Election, 2022, it was

Set 9.q: 101. The decision of the Supreme Court in the Indra Sawhney v. Union of India case is related to which subject?
options: Reservation for Other Backward Classes in government jobs
Approval of reservation in promotions for Scheduled Castes
Increase in reservation for Scheduled Tribes
Set 9.explanation: The decision of the nine-Judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992) is related to reservation for Other Backward Classes (OBCs) in government jobs. In this historic judgment, the Supreme Court upheld the government’s decision to provide 27 percent reservation to Other Backward Classes on the basis of the Mandal Commission report. However, it also held that the creamy layer, or the economically advanced section of the Other Backward Classes, should be kept outside its scope. Along with this, the Supreme Court also laid down that the total reservation provided under Articles 15(4) and 16(4) should not exceed the limit of 50 percent. Therefore, the correct answer is option (a).

Set 9.q: 102. No Money Bill can be introduced in the State Legislative Assembly without—
options: the recommendation of the Governor of the State
the recommendation of the President of India
the recommendation of a special committee of ministers
Set 9.explanation: Explanation: Under Article 207(1) of the Constitution, any Bill containing the provisions specified in sub-clauses (a) to (f) of clause (1) of Article 199, that is, a Money Bill, cannot be introduced in the State Legislative Assembly without the recommendation of the Governor of the State concerned. Therefore, the recommendation of the Governor of the State is necessary for introducing a Money Bill in the State Legislative Assembly. Thus, the correct answer is option (b).

Set 9.q: 103. In India, ‘judicial activism’ is related to—
Set 9.explanation: In India, “Judicial Activism” is related to both Judicial Review and Public Interest Litigation (PIL). However, in reality, judicial activism has emerged in India as a vehicle of social change mainly through the process of Public Interest Litigation. Therefore, among the given options, the most appropriate answer is option (b).

Set 9.q: 104. Consider the following statements regarding the President of India— (i) The Election Commission of India makes the final decision on any dispute related to the election of the President. (ii) Under Article 74, the President can dissolve the Lok Sabha. (iii) Any civil suit can be filed against the President. (iv) Impeachment of the President is a quasi-judicial process. (v) The President does not take part in the discussions in either House of Parliament.
Set 9.explanation: According to Article 71(1) of the Constitution, the final decision on any dispute related to the election of the President is made by the Supreme Court of India. Therefore, statement (i) is false. Under Article 85(2)(b), the President can dissolve the Lok Sabha. Therefore, statement (ii) is false. Under Article 361(4), a civil suit may be filed against the President or the Governor by giving two months’ prior notice. Therefore, statement (iii) is true. According to Article 61, impeachment of the President is a quasi-judicial process conducted in Parliament. Therefore, statement (iv) is correct. Under Article 79, the President is an integral part of Parliament. Under Article 87(1), at the beginning of the first session of each year, the President addresses both Houses of Parliament assembled together. However, the President does not take part in the discussion in either House. Therefore, statement (v) is correct. Thus, the required answer is option (c).

Set 9.q: 105. Which of the following is/are listed among the Directive Principles given in Part IV of the Indian Constitution? I. Equal pay for equal work II. Uniform Civil Code III. Small-family norm IV. Education in the mother tongue at the primary level
Set 9.explanation: Among the Directive Principles given in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, equal pay for equal work is listed in Article 39(d), and a Uniform Civil Code for citizens is listed in Article 44. Article 350A gives a special direction for providing facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage, although it is not included in Part IV. The small-family norm is also not listed in Part IV.

Set 9.q: 108. Consider the following statements— 1. The Chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. 2. The Public Accounts Committee includes members of the Lok Sabha, members of the Rajya Sabha and some well-known persons from industry and trade.
Set 9.explanation: The main function of the Public Accounts Committee is to examine the report of the Comptroller and Auditor General on the Appropriation Accounts of the Government of India. This committee has a total of 22 members. Of these, 15 members are elected from among the members of the Lok Sabha by the system of proportional representation through a single transferable vote, while seven members elected by the Rajya Sabha are associated with the Committee. No minister can be elected as a member of this committee. As per convention, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha appoints a leader from the Opposition as the Chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee. Hence, Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect, because there is no provision for selecting any outsider related to industry and trade, apart from members of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, in the Public Accounts Committee.

Set 9.q: 110. In which of the following types of forests is the maximum diversity of vascular plants found?
Set 9.explanation: Among the given options, the tropical evergreen forest biome has the highest number of species of vascular plants. This biome generally has a multi-layered structure, dense trees, shrubs and climbers. It provides the most favourable conditions for the growth and development of plants and animals, because it receives high rainfall and has high temperatures throughout the year.

Set 9.q: 111. Which one of the following is not responsible for increasing the biodiversity of an ecosystem?
Set 9.explanation: In an ecosystem, greater biodiversity develops when there is sufficient availability of energy and resources, the system has developed and remained stable for a long time, and the level of disturbance is moderate. Higher productivity increases the capacity to support more organisms and species. In ecosystems that have remained stable for a long period, species get more time for diversification and for the development of specialized niches. Similarly, moderate disturbance can prevent excessive dominance of any one species and promote the coexistence of many species. Trophic levels indicate the feeding position of organisms in a food chain, such as producers, herbivores, carnivores, etc. If the number of trophic levels is low, then the food chain and food web will be relatively simple. This may limit the diversity of ecological niches and groups of organisms instead of increasing it. Therefore, a smaller number of trophic levels is not responsible for an increase in biodiversity. Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

Set 9.q: 112. While making comprehensive reforms in the structure of the Wholesale Price Index (WPI), to which of the following has the Government of India changed its base year from 2011-12?
Set 9.explanation: The Government of India has approved the revision of the base year of the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) from 2011-12 to 2022-23. In the new WPI series, the number of items has been increased from 697 to 957.

Set 9.q: 113. Who is the Engagement Team Commander and Gender Focal Point with the Indian Battalion in the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL)...?
Set 9.explanation: Indian peacekeeper Major Abhilasha Barak has been honoured by the United Nations with the 2025 United Nations Military Gender Advocate of the Year Award. Set 9.q: 114. After the end of Jerome Powell’s term, who has taken charge as the new Chairman of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, which influences global financial markets?
Set 9.explanation: Kevin Warsh assumed charge as Chairman of the Board of Governors of the U.S. Federal Reserve System on May 22, 2026. He replaced Jerome Powell as Chairman. This position is extremely important from the point of view of global financial markets, because the monetary policy decisions of the U.S. Federal Reserve, especially those related to interest rates and financial conditions, affect not only the U.S. economy but also the world economy and global capital markets.

Set 9.q: 115. Neelam Meena was appointed by the Election Commission of India as the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) of which State in May 2026?
Set 9.explanation: Neelam Meena, a 1998-batch IAS officer of the West Bengal cadre, was appointed as the new Chief Electoral Officer of West Bengal. She replaced Manoj Kumar Agarwal. Set 9.q: 118. Consider the following statements regarding the ‘SARTHAK-PDS’ scheme approved to enhance transparency and security in the Public Distribution System: 1. Set 9.q: 119. In May 2026, from where was the country’s first indigenous ‘super-pressure balloon’ (SPB) launched, demonstrating the technological capability of high-altitude balloons?
options: Indira Gandhi Stadium, Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh

It was launched from Indira Gandhi Stadium, Vijayawada, Pradesh. The mission Andhra carried commercial payloads from seven national and international partners. VISTA reached an altitude of about 25 kilometres. Thus, the mission demonstrated India’s indigenous capability in stratospheric/near space balloon technology.

Set 9.q: 120. With reference to the passage of Uniform Civil Code (UCC) Bills, which of the following sequences of states is correct according to the historical order of their passage?
Set 9.explanation: In the chronological order of the passage of bills related to the Uniform Civil Code, Uttarakhand comes first, followed by Gujarat and then Assam. Subsequently, the Assam Assembly passed the Uniform Civil Code (Assam) Bill, 2026 on 27 May 2026. Thus, Assam became the third state in the country after Uttarakhand and Gujarat, and the first state in Northeast India, to pass such a Bill.

Set 9.q: 121. Recently, Randhir Singh passed away at the age of 79. Which of the following statements regarding him is incorrect?
options: He was the first sportsperson to win a gold medal for India in a shooting event at the Asian Games.
He had also served as the Secretary General of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA).
He remained active in various roles in the International Olympic Committee (IOC).
His birth and administrative work were mainly associated with the state of Bihar.

He served as the Secretary General of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) and held important positions in the International Olympic Committee (IOC) and the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA). Set 9.q: 123. In May 2026, President Droupadi Murmu presented the prestigious ‘President of India’s Police Colour’ to the police force of which state for outstanding service, courage and discipline?
Set 9.explanation: President Droupadi Murmu presented the ‘President of India’s Police Colour’ to the Sikkim Police at Paljor Stadium, Gangtok, on 28 May 2026. Set 9.q: 124. Padma Shri awardee and famous Urdu poet Bashir Badr recently passed away in Bhopal. Consider the following statements regarding him: 1. Bashir Badr’s real name was Syed Mohammad Bashir, and he was born in Ayodhya. 2. He had been suffering from a condition called dementia for the last 14 years.

He gave modern Urdu ghazal wide recognition through simple colloquial language and popular couplets. Therefore, both statements are correct.

Set 9.q: 125. Piyush Singla, a 2012-batch IAS officer of the AGMUT cadre, has recently been appointed as Director in which national mission/authority?
Set 9.explanation: Piyush Singla, a 2012-batch IAS officer of the AGMUT cadre, has been appointed Director in the National Health Authority under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission. The objective of the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission is to develop a secure, transparent and interoperable digital health ecosystem in the country.

Set 9.q: 126. Under the ‘ULLAS’ initiative of the Union Ministry of Education, which state has recently been officially declared a ‘Fully Literate State’?
Set 9.explanation: On 27 May 2026, during the seventh convocation ceremony of Sikkim University in Gangtok, Sikkim was officially declared a fully literate state. This achievement is linked to the ULLAS initiative of the Ministry of Education. ULLAS stands for Understanding of Lifelong Learning for All in Society. It is also called the New India Literacy Programme. In line with the National Education Policy 2020, this initiative aims to provide non-literate people aged 15 years and above with foundational literacy, numeracy, life skills and continuing education. Therefore, the correct answer is Sikkim.

Set 9.q: 127. On May 29, 2026, who took charge as the 48th Vice Chief of the Naval Staff (VCNS)?
Set 9.explanation: Vice Admiral Ajay Kochhar assumed charge as the 48th Vice Chief of the Naval Staff on 29 May 2026. He is an alumnus of the National Defence Academy, Pune, and was commissioned into the Indian Navy on 1 July 1988. Before becoming the VCNS, he served as the Commander-in-Chief, Andaman and Nicobar Command. Earlier, he had also served as the Commandant of the National Defence Academy. He was awarded the Ati Vishisht Seva Medal in 2022 and the Param Vishisht Seva Medal in 2026.

Set 9.q: 128. Nationalist leader Janez Janša has recently been elected as Prime Minister of which country for the fourth time?
Set 9.explanation: Nationalist/right-wing leader Janez Janša has been elected Prime Minister of Slovenia for the fourth time. He is the leader of the Slovenian Democratic Party (SDS). On 22 May 2026, he was elected Prime Minister by a 51–36 vote in Slovenia’s 90-member National Assembly. After this, on 4 June 2026, the cabinet of his centre-right coalition government was approved. He succeeded former Prime Minister Robert Golob.

Set 9.q: 129. Consider the following statements with reference to the Global Stock Market Rankings, 2026: 1. Taiwan’s stock market has surpassed India’s stock market to become the fifth-largest stock market in the world. 2. The main reason for Taiwan’s market surge has been the AI-driven semiconductor boom.
Set 9.explanation: In May 2026, Taiwan’s stock market overtook India in terms of market capitalisation and became the world’s fifth-largest equity market. At that time, Taiwan’s total market capitalisation was about US$4.95 trillion, while India’s was about US$4.92 trillion. The main reason for Taiwan’s rise was the strong demand for semiconductors related to artificial intelligence and high-performance computing, along with a sharp rise in technology stocks, including TSMC. Therefore, both statements are true.

Set 9.q: 130. Which Indian female athlete won the gold medal after breaking the 14-year-old national high jump record at the Asian U20 Athletics Championships 2026 held in Hong Kong?
Set 9.explanation: Indian high jumper Pooja Singh won the gold medal at the 22nd Asian Under-20 Athletics Championships 2026, held in Hong Kong, with a jump of 1.93 metres. With this performance, she broke the senior women’s national high jump record of 1.92 metres set by Sahana Kumari in 2012. In the same event, Pooja also improved the Asian Under-20 Championships meet record. She had also won the high jump gold medal at the senior Asian Athletics Championships in 2025.

Set 9.q: 131. After the completion of Dr. Samir V. Kamat’s tenure, who was given additional charge as Chairman of the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)?
Set 9.explanation: Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh has been assigned the additional charge of Secretary, Department of Defence Research and Development, and Chairman, Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO). This additional charge was assigned after the tenure of Dr. Samir V. Kamat ended on 31 May 2026. This arrangement will continue until the appointment of a regular incumbent or until further orders. Rajesh Kumar Singh is a 1989-batch IAS officer of the Kerala cadre.

Set 9.q: 132. The new book “India’s First Olympic Gold”, written by renowned hockey historian K. Arumugam and recently released by P. T. Usha, is based on India’s journey at which historic Olympic Games?
Set 9.explanation: “India’s First Olympic Gold” is a book written by renowned hockey historian K. Arumugam. This book is based on the historic journey of the Indian men’s hockey team winning India’s first Olympic gold medal at the 1928 Amsterdam Olympics. This victory marked the beginning of the golden era of Indian hockey and established Dhyan Chand as one of the greats of world hockey.

Set 9.q: 133. Where was the first multilateral military exercise ‘PRAGATI 2026’ held in May 2026 among the armies of 13 countries of the Indian Ocean Region?
Set 9.explanation: In May 2026, the first multilateral military exercise ‘PRAGATI 2026’ was held at Umroi Military Station, Meghalaya. More than 400 soldiers from India and friendly countries—Bhutan, Cambodia, Malaysia, Maldives, Myanmar, Nepal, the Philippines, Seychelles, Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Indonesia and Laos—participated in it. This exercise focused on strengthening counter-terrorism operations in semi-mountainous and jungle terrain, interoperability, mutual trust, collective preparedness and military-to-military cooperation.

Set 9.q: 134. In which city was the Indian Navy’s Open-Air Display Museum ‘Nausena Shaurya Vatika’ jointly inaugurated by Union Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh?
Set 9.explanation: Explanation: Union Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath jointly inaugurated ‘Nausena Shaurya Vatika’ in Lucknow on 30 May 2026. This Open-Air Display Museum has been developed at a cost of Rs 19 crore over an area of more than two acres. It has been prepared under the second phase of the Nausena Shaurya Sangrahalaya. Artefacts related to INS Gomati, weapon systems, radar, torpedo launcher, anchors and other naval equipment have been displayed in it. This Vatika is an inspirational place that conveys the tradition of bravery, valour and national service of the Indian Navy to the general public, especially the youth.

Set 9.q: 135. With reference to ‘World Milk Day, 2026’, observed on 1 June, consider the following statements: 1. The official theme of World Milk Day for the year 2026 was “Celebrating Women Farmers”. 2. World Milk Day was initiated in the year 2001 by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) of the United Nations.
Set 9.explanation: World Milk Day is celebrated every year on 1 June. Its objective is to raise awareness about the contribution of milk and the dairy sector to nutrition, food security, rural livelihood and economic development. In 2026, the theme of World Milk Day was “Celebrating Women Farmers”, which highlights the important role of women farmers in the dairy sector and agri-food systems. World Milk Day was initiated in 2001 by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) of the United Nations. Set 9.q: 136. Under the recently implemented Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Ordinance, 2026, the Central Government has appointed five new judges to the Supreme Court. Under this who among the following became one of the few women lawyers to be directly elevated from the Bar to the Supreme Court Bench?
Set 9.explanation: On 1 June 2026, the President appointed Justice Sheel Nagu, Justice Shree Chandrashekhar, Justice Sanjeev Sachdeva, Justice Arun Palli and Senior Advocate V. Mohana as new judges of the Supreme Court under Article 124(2) of the Constitution. Among them, Senior Advocate V. Mohana is especially notable because she became the second woman advocate to be appointed directly from the Supreme Court Bar as a judge of the Supreme Court. Before her, in 2018, Senior Advocate Indu Malhotra was appointed directly from the Bar as a Supreme Court judge. After the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Ordinance, 2026, the sanctioned strength of judges in the Supreme Court increased from 33 to 37, excluding the Chief Justice; including the CJI, the total sanctioned strength became 38.

Set 9.q: 137. Major General Rachel Thomas assumed charge as Additional Director General (ADG) of which prestigious military service on 1 June, 2026?
Set 9.explanation: Major General Rachel Thomas assumed charge as Additional Director General (ADG) of the Military Nursing Service (MNS) on 1 June 2026. She succeeded Major General Lissamma PV, who retired on 31 May 2026. She is an alumna of the College of Nursing, Armed Forces Medical College (AFMC), Pune. She was commissioned into the Military Nursing Service on 1 June 1988.

Set 9.q: 138. Which university has earned the distinction of becoming the country’s first ‘Microsoft GenAI Campus’ through a global technology partnership with Microsoft and Google Cloud?
Set 9.explanation: GLA University, located in Mathura, Uttar Pradesh, has earned the distinction of becoming India’s first Microsoft GenAI Campus. The university has taken the initiative to provide students with advanced technical skills, hands-on learning and industry-oriented exposure through an artificial intelligence and cloud-learning ecosystem based on Microsoft and Google/Google Cloud. GLA University is also described as North India’s first Google Agentic AI University. This initiative is important from the perspective of skill development based on AI, cloud computing and digital innovation.

Set 9.q: 139. Which new zone officially began operations on 1 June, 2026 as the 18th railway zone of Indian Railways, with its headquarters located in Visakhapatnam?
Set 9.explanation: From 1 June 2026, the South Coast Railway (SCoR) zone became functional as the 18th railway zone of Indian Railways. Its headquarters is located in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh. This new zone has been formed from reorganized areas of the existing East Coast Railway and South Central Railway. It includes Vijayawada, Guntur, Guntakal and the reorganized Visakhapatnam Division.

Set 9.q: 140. Which team won the Indian Premier League (IPL) title for the second consecutive season by defeating Gujarat Titans in the final match played on 31 May, 2026?
Set 9.explanation: In the IPL 2026 final played at Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad, on 31 May 2026, Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) defeated Gujarat Titans (GT) by 5 wickets. With this victory, RCB successfully defended its title by winning the IPL title in 2026 as well, after 2025. Virat Kohli was chosen as Player of the Match for his unbeaten innings of 75 runs off 42 balls. RCB received prize money of Rs 20 crore as the winner. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi won the Orange Cap by scoring 776 runs, while Kagiso Rabada won the Purple Cap by taking 29 wickets.

Set 10.q: 1. Which of the following duties is not included among the Fundamental Duties of a citizen?
options: To protect and improve the natural environment
To cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom
To make efforts towards abolishing untouchability
To develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform
Set 10.explanation: Fundamental Duties are included in Article 51A under Part IVA of the Indian Constitution. Making efforts to eradicate untouchability is not included in these duties. The abolition of untouchability under Article 17 is a Fundamental Right.

Set 10.q: 2. Which one of the following is not included in the Directive Principles of State Policy?
options: There is equal pay for equal work for both men and women
Men and women have an equal right to an adequate means of livelihood
There are just and humane conditions of work
Set 10.explanation: Under the Fundamental Rights in the Constitution, the abolition of untouchability is mentioned in Article 17 under the Right to Equality. Among the other three options, equal pay for equal work for both men and women is given in Article 39(d), the equal right to an adequate means of livelihood is given in Article 39(a), and just and humane conditions of work are given in Article 42. These come under the Directive Principles of State Policy.

Set 10.q: 3. Consider the following statements: 1. The Council of Ministers at the Centre shall be collectively responsible to Parliament. 2. Union Ministers shall hold office during the pleasure of the President of India. 3. The Prime Minister shall communicate the proposals for legislation to the President.
Set 10.explanation: According to Article 75(3) of the Constitution, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha and not to Parliament, which includes the President, the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha. According to Article 75(2), Ministers shall hold office during the pleasure of the President. According to Article 78(a), it is the duty of the Prime Minister to communicate to the President all decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to the administration of the affairs of the Union and proposals for legislation.

Set 10.q: 4. Which of the following does the President appoint?
Set 10.explanation: In the Indian Constitution, the President has been given the power to make appointments to several constitutional posts. According to Article 76(1), the Attorney-General for India is appointed by the President. According to Article 148(1), the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India is appointed by the President. Similarly, according to Article 155, the Governor of a State is also appointed by the President. Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

Set 10.q: 5. The National Development Council— 1. Discusses the progress of the National Plan. 2. Suggests measures for achieving the objectives of the National Plan. 3. Provides guidelines for the formulation of the National Plan. 4. Suggests the allocation of funds in the Plan.
Set 10.explanation: The main functions of the National Development Council are as follows— (i) To provide guidelines for the preparation of the National Plan and also to assess the resources for the Plan. (ii) To consider the National Plan prepared by the Planning Com mission. (iii) To consider social and economic issues affecting national develop ment. (iv) To review the working of the Plan from time to time and to give advice for achieving the objectives of the National Plan. The work of suggesting the allocation of funds in the Plan was done by the then Planning Commission and not by the National Development Council. Hence, the correct answer will be option (a).

Set 10.q: 6. Match the following correctly— A. Article 243Q B. Article 243T C. Article 243J D. Article 243C | 1. Reservation of seats in Municipalities 2. Audit of accounts of Panchayats 3. Constitution of Municipalities 4. Composition of Panchayats
Set 10.explanation: The correct matching is as follows— Article 243Q – Constitution of Municipalities Article 243T – Reservation of seats in Municipalities Article 243J – Audit of accounts of Panchayats Article 243C – Composition of Panchayats

Set 10.q: 7. Which one of the following statements related to the Rajya Sabha is correct?
options: The Rajya Sabha is not subject to dissolution.
Its members are elected by direct election from territorial constituencies in the States.
The Rajya Sabha, as soon as possible, elects one of its members as its Chairman.
The Attorney-General for India has no right to speak in the Rajya Sabha.
Set 10.explanation: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House. It is not dissolved. The term of its members is 6 years and, as far as possible, one-third of its members are indirectly elected every two years by the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States. Also, the Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and the Attorney-General has the right to speak in both Houses of Parliament. Therefore, the correct answer is option (a).

Set 10.q: 9. Match List-I with List-II: A. Fundamental Rights B. Directive Principles of State Policy C. Cabinet Government D. Centre-State Relations | i. British Constitution ii. Constitution of Canada iii. Irish Constitution iv. American Bill of Rights
Set 10.explanation: The correct matching is as follows— List-I (Constitutional Provision) Fundamental Rights Directive Principles of State Policy List-II (Source) American Bill of Rights Irish Constitution Cabinet Government British Con stitution Centre-State Relations Constitution of Canada

Set 10.q: 10. A parliamentary system of government is one in which—
options: All political parties in Parliament are represented in the government.
The government is responsible to the Lok Sabha and can be removed by it.
The government is elected by the people and can be removed by them.
The government is elected by Parliament, but cannot be removed before the completion of its fixed term.
Set 10.explanation: A parliamentary system of government is one in which the government is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha and can be removed by it. The Indian Constitution has established a parliamentary system of government. It is inspired by the parliamentary system of England. Therefore, in a parliamentary system, the existence of the government depends not on being removed directly by the people, but on the confidence of the elected House. Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

Set 10.q: 11. In which of the following matters is it not necessary for the President to take the advice of the Council of Ministers?
options: Giving assent to Bills forwarded by the Governor
Set 10.explanation: It is not necessary for the President to take the advice of the Council of Ministers for giving assent to Bills. Article 111 of the Constitution states that when an ordinary Bill, after being passed by the Houses of Parliament, is presented to the President, the President shall declare either that he gives assent to the Bill or that he withholds assent, though no time limit has been fixed in this regard, or the President may return the Bill to the Houses for reconsideration. If the Bill is again passed by the Houses, with or without amendments, and is presented to the President for assent, then the President shall not withhold assent from it.

Set 10.q: 12. Which one of the following motions can the Council of Ministers move in India?
Set 10.explanation: In Parliament, a Motion of Confidence is moved by the government as a motion seeking support. Such a motion is passed or rejected only in Parliament, that is, in the Lok Sabha. The government brings a Motion of Confidence in the Lok Sabha only when it has to prove its majority in the Lok Sabha. A Motion of Confidence may be moved by the Prime Minister, the Council of Ministers, or any one of its members, whereas a No-Confidence Motion against the government in the Lok Sabha is brought by a member of the Opposition.

Set 10.q: 13. Who among the following was the Chairman of the Union Constitution Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
Set 10.explanation: The major committees of the Constituent Assembly and their Chairmen were as follows— Union Constitution Committee – Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru Committee on the Rules of Procedure – Dr. Rajendra Prasad Steering Committee – Dr. Rajendra Prasad Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal and Excluded Areas – Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee – J.B. Kripalani Minorities Sub-Committee – H.C. Mookherjee Provincial Constitution Committee – Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Order of Business Committee – K.M. Munshi

Set 10.q: 14. Rajya Sabha members are not included in— 1. Public Accounts Committee 2. Estimates Committee 3. Committee on Public Undertakings
Set 10.explanation: All 30 members of the Estimates Committee are drawn from the Lok Sabha, and Rajya Sabha members are not included in it. On the other hand, in both the Public Accounts Committee and the Committee on Public Undertakings, 15 members are elected from the Lok Sabha and 7 members from the Rajya Sabha. The Committee on Government Assurances is constituted separately in both Houses; the Lok Sabha Committee has 15 members and the Rajya Sabha Committee has 10 members.

Set 10.q: 15. Who among the following attends the meetings of the Public Accounts Committee of Parliament?
options: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
Set 10.explanation: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India attends the meetings of the Public Accounts Committee of Parliament and assists the Committee in its deliberations. The Public Accounts Committee mainly examines the Appropriation Accounts, the Finance Accounts, and the reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General. Article 149 of the Constitution lays down the duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor General. Therefore, the correct answer to this question is the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.

Set 10.q: 16. Which of the following statements regarding the Rajya Sabha is/are correct? 1. It cannot be dissolved. 2. Its term is five years. 3. Every two years, the term of one-third of its members comes to an end. 4. Its members shall not be less than 25 years of age.
Set 10.explanation: The Rajya Sabha is called the Upper House and the Permanent House of Parliament. Unlike the Lok Sabha, the Rajya Sabha is not dissolved. Therefore, statement 1 is correct. The Rajya Sabha is not constituted for a term of five years; the normal term of its members is six years. Therefore, statement 2 is incorrect. To maintain and culture.
